title.raw: 卷102 西域 Volume 102: Western Regions

sentences.zh: 夏書稱「西戎即序」，班固云：就而序之，非盛威武，致其貢物也。

translations.literal: The Documents of Xia says, "The Western Rong are brought into order"; Ban Gu says: to bring them into order where they are—not to display martial might in order to obtain their tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Xia speaks of the Western barbarians being "brought into order," and Ban Gu explains that this meant arranging them in their places—not flaunting military power merely to extract tribute.

sentences.zh: 漢氏初開西域，有三十六國。

translations.literal: When the Han house first opened the Western Regions, there were thirty-six states.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty first opened contact with the Western Regions, there were thirty-six kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 其後分立五十五王，置校尉、都護以撫納之。

translations.literal: Later they were divided into fifty-five kings; colonels and protectors-general were installed to pacify and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the region was split among fifty-five rulers, and the court appointed colonels and protectors-general to win them over and keep them in line.

sentences.zh: 王莽篡位，西域遂絕。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang usurped the throne, contact with the Western Regions was severed.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Mang seized the throne, ties with the Western Regions were cut off.

sentences.zh: 至於後漢，班超所通者五十餘國，西至西海，東西萬里，皆來朝貢，復置都護、校尉以相統攝。

translations.literal: In Later Han, the states reached by Ban Chao numbered more than fifty; west to the Western Sea, ten thousand li east and west—all came to court with tribute; protectors-general and colonels were again installed to oversee them jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Han, Ban Chao reconnected more than fifty states stretching west to the Western Sea—ten thousand li from east to west—all of which sent tribute. The court again appointed protectors-general and colonels to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 其後或絕或通，漢朝以為勞弊中國，其官時置時廢。

translations.literal: Afterward contact was sometimes severed and sometimes restored; the Han court considered it a drain that exhausted China, and these offices were at times established and at times abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter ties were intermittent; the Han court regarded the enterprise as a burden that wore down the empire, and the frontier offices were created and abolished by turns.

sentences.zh: 暨魏晉之後，互相吞滅，不可復詳記焉。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, they swallowed one another and can no longer be recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei and Jin periods the states devoured one another until their history can no longer be traced in full.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，經營中原，未暇及於四表。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Grand Ancestor's reign, he was consolidating the Central Plains and had no leisure for the four peripheries.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years of Emperor Daowu, he was busy securing the Central Plains and had no time for the distant frontiers.

sentences.zh: 既而西戎之貢不至，有司奏依漢氏故事，請通西域，可以振威德於荒外，又可致奇貨於天府。

translations.literal: Before long tribute from the Western Rong ceased to arrive; the responsible officials memorialized that, following Han precedent, the Western Regions should be reopened—this could extend prestige and virtue to the wild beyond, and also bring rare goods into the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute from the western peoples stopped arriving, officials urged reopening the Western Regions along Han lines, arguing that it would project imperial prestige beyond the frontier and channel exotic goods into the state coffers.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「漢氏不保境安人，乃遠開西域，使海內虛耗，何利之有？

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor said: "The Han house did not secure its borders and settle its people, yet opened the Western Regions far away, draining the realm within—what profit was there in that?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu replied: "The Han failed to secure their borders and protect their people, yet still pushed into the distant west and emptied the empire—what good did that do?

sentences.zh: 今若通之，前弊復加百姓矣。」

translations.literal: If we open contact now, the former evils will again be imposed on the common people."
translations.idiomatic: If we reopen those routes now, the same burdens will fall on the people again."

sentences.zh: 遂不從。

translations.literal: He did not follow the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 歷太宗世，竟不招納。

translations.literal: Throughout the reign of the Founding Ancestor, they were never recruited or received.
translations.idiomatic: Through Emperor Mingyuan's entire reign, the court never sought to bring them in.

sentences.zh: 太延中，魏德益以遠聞，西域龜茲、疏勒、烏孫、悅般、渴槃陁、鄯善、焉耆、車師、粟特諸國王始遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the Taiyan era, Wei virtue was increasingly heard afar; the kings of Kucha, Kashgar, Wusun, Yueban, Khotan, Shanshan, Karashahr, Cheshi, and Sogdiana in the Western Regions first sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyan period, Wei prestige spread ever farther; rulers of Kucha, Kashgar, Wusun, Yueban, Khotan, Shanshan, Karashahr, Cheshi, Sogdiana, and other western states began sending embassies with tribute.

sentences.zh: 世祖以西域漢世雖通，有求則卑辭而來，無欲則驕慢王命，此其自知絕遠，大兵不可至故也。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor considered that although the Western Regions had contact in Han times, when they had requests they came with humble words, and when they had no desire they were arrogant toward imperial commands—this was because they knew themselves to be utterly remote and that great armies could not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu observed that even in Han times the western states came obsequiously when they wanted something and grew insolent toward imperial orders when they did not—knowing how remote they were and that no great army could reach them.

sentences.zh: 若報使往來，終無所益，欲不遣使。

translations.literal: If envoys were exchanged in return, in the end there would be no benefit; he wished not to send envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Exchanging embassies would ultimately gain nothing, he thought, and he was inclined not to send any.

sentences.zh: 有司奏九國不憚遐嶮，遠貢方物，當與其進，安可豫抑後來，乃從之。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized that the nine states did not fear the distant barriers but brought local products from afar—they should be met in their advance; how could one prematurely restrain those who came later? He followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued that the nine kingdoms had braved immense distances to offer tribute and deserved encouragement—not preemptive discouragement of others who might follow. He agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是始遣行人王恩生、許綱等西使，恩生出流沙，為蠕蠕所執，竟不果達。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first sent the traveling envoy Wang Ensheng, Xu Gang, and others on a western mission; Ensheng went beyond the shifting sands and was seized by the Rouran, and in the end did not succeed in arriving.
translations.idiomatic: The court then dispatched Wang Ensheng, Xu Gang, and other envoys westward; beyond the desert sands Ensheng was captured by the Rouran and never reached his destination.

sentences.zh: 又遣散騎侍郎董琬、高明等多齎錦帛，出鄯善，招撫九國，厚賜之。

translations.literal: He also sent Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Dong Wan, Gao Ming, and others bearing much silk and brocade; they went out through Shanshan to win over and pacify the nine states, generously bestowing gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He next sent Dong Wan, Gao Ming, and others of the scattered-cavalry staff with lavish silks, routing through Shanshan to court the nine states with rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 初，琬等受詔，便道之國可往赴之。

translations.literal: At first, when Wan and the others received the edict, they were to go by convenient routes to whichever states they could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and his party had orders to take whatever routes would let them visit whichever states lay along the way.

sentences.zh: 琬過九國，北行至烏孫國，其王得朝廷所賜，拜受甚悅，謂琬曰：「傳聞破洛那、者舌皆思魏德，欲稱臣致貢，但患其路無由耳。

translations.literal: Wan passed through the nine states and went north to the state of Wusun; its king received what the court had bestowed, bowed in acceptance, and was greatly pleased. He said to Wan: "I have heard that Poluona and Zhe She both yearn for Wei virtue and wish to submit and send tribute, but they only worry that there is no route.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the nine states Wan traveled north to Wusun. The king, delighted with the imperial gifts, told him: "We hear that Ferghana and the lands beyond the Pamirs both admire Wei and wish to submit tribute—they only lack a road.

sentences.zh: 今使君等既到此，可往二國，副其慕仰之誠。」

translations.literal: Now that you envoys have come here, you may go to the two states and fulfill their sincere admiration."
translations.idiomatic: Since you envoys have come this far, you might visit those two lands and answer their longing."

sentences.zh: 琬於是自向破洛那，遣明使者舌。

translations.literal: Wan thereupon went himself toward Poluona and sent Ming as envoy to Zhe She.
translations.idiomatic: Wan then went on to Ferghana himself and dispatched Ming toward the Pamir region.

sentences.zh: 烏孫王為發導譯達二國，琬等宣詔慰賜之。

translations.literal: The king of Wusun provided guides and interpreters to reach the two states; Wan and the others proclaimed the edict, comforted them, and bestowed gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Wusun king furnished guides and interpreters; Wan proclaimed the imperial edict, offered reassurance, and distributed gifts.

sentences.zh: 已而琬、明東還，烏孫、破洛那之屬遣使與琬俱來貢獻者十有六國。

translations.literal: Before long Wan and Ming returned east; Wusun, Poluona, and their kind sent envoys who came with Wan to present tribute—sixteen states in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan and Ming returned eastward, envoys from Wusun, Ferghana, and related states accompanied them—sixteen kingdoms in all.

sentences.zh: 自後相繼而來，不間于歲，國使亦數十輩矣。

translations.literal: From then on they came in succession without a year's gap; foreign envoys also numbered several tens of missions.
translations.idiomatic: After that embassies arrived year after year without interruption—dozens of missions in all.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖每遣使西域，常詔河西王沮渠牧犍令護送，至姑臧，牧犍恒發使導路出於流沙。

translations.literal: At first, whenever the Shizu Emperor sent envoys to the Western Regions, he regularly ordered the King of Hexi, Juqu Mujian, to escort them; when they reached Guzang, Mujian always sent men to guide the route beyond the shifting sands.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, whenever Emperor Taiwu sent missions westward, he ordered the Hexi king Juqu Mujian to escort them; at Guzang, Mujian routinely provided guides across the desert.

sentences.zh: 後使者自西域還，至武威，牧犍左右謂使者曰：「我君承蠕蠕吳提妄說，云：『去歲魏天子自來伐我，士馬疫死，大敗而還，我禽其長弟樂平王丕。』

translations.literal: Later, when envoys returned from the Western Regions and reached Wuwei, men about Mujian said to the envoys: "Our lord has accepted the false tale of the Rouran khan Wuti, who says: 'Last year the Wei Son of Heaven came in person to attack me; men and horses died of pestilence; he was utterly defeated and retreated; I captured his elder younger brother, the Prince of Leping, Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys returning from the west reached Wuwei, Mujian's attendants told them: "Our lord believes the Rouran khan Wuti's boast that last year the Wei emperor marched against him in person, that his army was ravaged by disease and routed, and that Wuti captured the emperor's brother, Prince Pi of Leping.

sentences.zh: 我君大喜，宣言國中。」

translations.literal: Our lord was greatly pleased and proclaimed it throughout the state."
translations.idiomatic: Our lord was overjoyed and proclaimed it throughout his realm."

sentences.zh: 又聞吳提遣使告西域諸國，稱：「魏已削弱，今天下唯我為強，若更有魏使，勿復恭奉。」

translations.literal: It was also heard that Wuti sent envoys to tell the states of the Western Regions, declaring: "Wei is already weakened; today under Heaven only I am strong—if there are further Wei envoys, do not again respect and serve them."
translations.idiomatic: They also heard that Wuti had told the western states: "Wei is weakened; I alone am supreme—if more Wei envoys come, do not defer to them again."

sentences.zh: 西域諸國亦有貳者。

translations.literal: Among the states of the Western Regions there were also those who wavered in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Some western states wavered in their allegiance.

sentences.zh: 牧犍事主稍以慢惰。

translations.literal: Mujian's service to his sovereign gradually grew slack and negligent.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian's loyalty to the Wei court grew increasingly lax.

sentences.zh: 使還，具以狀聞，世祖遂議討牧犍。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, they reported the full situation; the Shizu Emperor thereupon deliberated on attacking Mujian.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys reported everything on their return, and Emperor Taiwu resolved to punish Mujian.

sentences.zh: 涼州既平，鄯善國以為「脣亡齒寒，自然之道也，今武威為魏所滅，次及我也。

translations.literal: After Liang province was pacified, the state of Shanshan reasoned: "When the lips are gone the teeth grow cold—this is the natural way; now Wuwei has been destroyed by Wei, and I will be next.
translations.idiomatic: After Liangzhou fell, Shanshan concluded: "When the lips perish the teeth freeze—that is nature's law. Wuwei is gone; we are next.

sentences.zh: 若通其使人，知我國事，取亡必近，不如絕之，可以支久」，乃斷塞行路，西域貢獻，歷年不入。

translations.literal: If we let their envoys pass and they learn our state's affairs, our destruction will soon be near—it is better to cut them off so we can endure long." They therefore blocked and sealed the routes; tribute from the Western Regions did not enter for years."
translations.idiomatic: If we let their envoys through and they learn our weakness, ruin will come quickly. Better to cut the roads and hold out." They blocked the routes, and western tribute ceased for years."

sentences.zh: 後平鄯善，行人復通。

translations.literal: Later, when Shanshan was pacified, traveling envoys were again able to pass.
translations.idiomatic: After Shanshan was subdued, diplomatic traffic resumed.

sentences.zh: 始琬等使還京師，具言凡所經見及傳聞傍國，云：西域自漢武時五十餘國，後稍相并。

translations.literal: When Wan and the others first returned to the capital, they reported in full everything they had seen and heard about neighboring states, saying: From Emperor Wu of Han's time there were more than fifty states in the Western Regions; later they gradually annexed one another.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital, Wan's party described all they had seen and heard: in Han Wudi's day the west held more than fifty states, which later merged through conquest.

sentences.zh: 至太延中，為十六國，分其地為四域。

translations.literal: By the Taiyan era there were sixteen states, and their territory was divided into four regions.
translations.idiomatic: By the Taiyan period only sixteen kingdoms remained, grouped into four regions.

sentences.zh: 自葱嶺以東，流沙以西為一域；

translations.literal: From the Pamirs east to the shifting sands west formed one region;
translations.idiomatic: East of the Pamirs and west of the desert formed one region;

sentences.zh: 葱嶺以西，海曲以東為一域；

translations.literal: west of the Pamirs and east of the sea's bend formed one region;
translations.idiomatic: west of the Pamirs and east of the sea's curve formed another;

sentences.zh: 者舌以南，月氏以北為一域；

translations.literal: south of Zhe She and north of the Yuezhi formed one region;
translations.idiomatic: south of the Pamir passes and north of the Yuezhi formed a third;

sentences.zh: 兩海之間，水澤以南為一域。

translations.literal: between the two seas, south of the marshes and waters, formed one region.
translations.idiomatic: between the two seas, south of the lakes and marshes, formed the fourth.

sentences.zh: 內諸小渠長蓋以百數。

translations.literal: The lesser chieftains and canal heads within probably numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Petty chiefs within those regions likely numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 其出西域本有二道，後更為四：出自玉門，渡流沙，西行二千里至鄯善為一道；

translations.literal: The routes out of the Western Regions were originally two, later becoming four: from Yumen Pass, crossing the shifting sands, west two thousand li to Shanshan was one route;
translations.idiomatic: Routes westward were originally two, later four: from Yumen Pass across the sands, two thousand li west to Shanshan was the first;

sentences.zh: 自玉門渡流沙，北行二千二百里至車師為一道；

translations.literal: from Yumen crossing the shifting sands, north two thousand two hundred li to Cheshi was one route;
translations.idiomatic: from Yumen north across the sands, twenty-two hundred li to Cheshi was the second;

sentences.zh: 從莎車西行一百里至葱嶺，葱嶺西一千三百里至伽倍為一道；

translations.literal: from Shache west one hundred li to the Pamirs, and west of the Pamirs one thousand three hundred li to Jiabei was one route;
translations.idiomatic: from Shache west one hundred li to the Pamirs, then thirteen hundred li beyond to Kabadi was the third;

sentences.zh: 自莎車西南五百里葱嶺，西南一千三百里至波路為一道焉。

translations.literal: from Shache southwest five hundred li to the Pamirs, and southwest of the Pamirs one thousand three hundred li to Bolu was one route.
translations.idiomatic: from Shache southwest five hundred li to the Pamirs, then thirteen hundred li southwest to Bolu was the fourth.

sentences.zh: 自琬所不傳而更有朝貢者，紀其名，不能具國俗也。

translations.literal: As for those who sent tribute but were not reported by Wan, their names are recorded; their national customs cannot be given in full.
translations.idiomatic: States that sent tribute but lay outside Wan's route are named here; their customs are not described in detail.

sentences.zh: 其與前使所異者錄之。

translations.literal: What differs from earlier envoys' reports is recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Where their accounts differ from earlier missions, that is noted.

sentences.zh: 鄯善國，都扜泥城，[2]古樓蘭國也。

translations.literal: The state of Shanshan has its capital at Qianni City—it is the ancient state of Loulan.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Shanshan, capital at Qianni, is the old land of Loulan.

sentences.zh: 去代七千六百里，所都城方一里。

translations.literal: It is seven thousand six hundred li from Dai; its walled city is one li square.
translations.idiomatic: It lies seventy-six hundred li from the Wei capital; its city walls enclose one square li.

sentences.zh: 地多沙鹵，少水草，北即白龍堆路。

translations.literal: The land has much saline sand and little water and grass; to the north is the route of the White Dragon Mounds.
translations.idiomatic: The soil is salty and barren, water and pasture scarce; to the north lies the White Dragon Mounds route.

sentences.zh: 至太延初，始遣使來獻。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Taiyan, they first sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiyan era they first sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣其弟素延耆入侍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, they sent the king's younger brother Su Yanqi to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the king sent his brother Su Yanqi to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 及世祖平涼州，沮渠牧犍弟無諱走保敦煌。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor pacified Liang province, Juqu Mujian's younger brother Wuhui fled to hold Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu conquered Liangzhou, Juqu Mujian's brother Wuhui retreated to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 無諱後謀渡流沙，遣其弟安周擊鄯善，王比龍恐懼欲降。

translations.literal: Wuhui later planned to cross the shifting sands and sent his younger brother Anzhou to attack Shanshan; King Bilong was afraid and wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhui later planned to cross the desert and sent his brother Anzhou against Shanshan; King Bilong, terrified, was ready to submit.

sentences.zh: 會魏使者自天竺、罽賓還，俱會鄯善，勸比龍拒之，遂與連戰，安周不能克，退保東城。

translations.literal: It happened that Wei envoys returning from India and Kashmir all met at Shanshan and urged Bilong to resist; they then fought in succession; Anzhou could not overcome them and withdrew to hold the eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei envoys returning from India and Kashmir happened to arrive and urged Bilong to resist. After repeated battles Anzhou failed to take the city and fell back to the eastern quarter.

sentences.zh: 後比龍懼，率眾西奔且末，其世子乃應安周。

translations.literal: Later Bilong was afraid and led his people west in flight to Qiemo; his heir then went over to Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bilong later fled west to Qiemo with his followers; his crown prince then sided with Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄯善人頗剽劫之，[3]令不得通。

translations.literal: The people of Shanshan rather plundered and robbed, so that passage was not possible.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshan raiders harassed travelers until the routes were impassable.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔散騎常侍、成周公萬度歸乘傳發涼州兵討之，度歸到敦煌，留輜重，以輕騎五千渡流沙，至其境。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor ordered Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Duke of Cheng, Wan Dugui, traveling post-haste, to mobilize Liang province troops to attack them. Dugui reached Dunhuang, left the baggage train, and with five thousand light cavalry crossed the shifting sands into their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu ordered Wan Dugui, Duke of Cheng, to march Liangzhou troops against them. At Dunhuang he left his baggage and crossed the desert with five thousand light horse.

sentences.zh: 時鄯善人眾布野，度歸敕吏卒不得有所侵掠，邊守感之，皆望旗稽服。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Shanshan were scattered in the wilds; Dugui ordered officials and soldiers not to plunder at all; the frontier guards were moved by this and all looked to the banners and bowed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshan's people were scattered across the countryside; Dugui forbade looting, and the border garrisons, impressed, surrendered at sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 其王真達面縛出降，度歸釋其縛，留軍屯守，與真達詣京都。

translations.literal: Their king Zhenda came out bound, his face covered, to surrender; Dugui released his bonds, left troops to garrison and hold the place, and went with Zhenda to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhenda came out bound in surrender; Dugui freed him, left a garrison, and escorted him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世祖大悅，厚待之。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor was greatly pleased and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was delighted and received him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，拜交趾公韓拔為假節、[4]征西將軍、領護西戎校尉、鄯善王以鎮之，賦役其人，比之郡縣。

translations.literal: That year, Duke of Jiaozhi Han Ba was appointed with provisional credentials, General Who Conquers the West, and concurrently Colonel Protecting the Western Rong and King of Shanshan to garrison it; levies and corvée were imposed on the people, comparable to commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: That year Han Ba was made acting commissioner, General Who Conquers the West, protector of the western peoples, and king of Shanshan to hold the region; its people were taxed and drafted like subjects of interior commanderies.

sentences.zh: 且末國，都且末城，在鄯善西，去代八千三百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Qiemo has its capital at Qiemo City; it lies west of Shanshan, eight thousand three hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Qiemo, capital at Qiemo city, lies west of Shanshan, eighty-three hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 真君三年，鄯善王比龍避沮渠安周之難，率國人之半奔且末，後役屬鄯善。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenjun, the king of Shanshan, Bilong, fleeing the trouble of Juqu Anzhou, led half the state's people in flight to Qiemo; later they were subordinated and attached to Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun year three, fleeing Juqu Anzhou, King Bilong brought half his people to Qiemo; they later fell under Shanshan's control.

sentences.zh: 且末西北方流沙數百里，夏日有熱風為行旅之患。

translations.literal: Northwest of Qiemo the shifting sands extend several hundred li; in summer there are hot winds that are a scourge to travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Qiemo lie hundreds of li of desert where summer brings scorching winds deadly to travelers.

sentences.zh: 風之所至，唯老駝豫知之，即鳴而聚立，埋其口鼻於沙中，人每以為候，亦即將氈擁蔽鼻口。

translations.literal: Where the wind is about to strike, only old camels know beforehand; they immediately cry out and gather standing, burying their muzzles in the sand—people take this as a sign and likewise wrap felt over their noses and mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Only veteran camels sense the wind in advance; they bellow and cluster, burying their snouts in the sand. Travelers take this as warning and wrap felt over their faces.

sentences.zh: 其風迅駛，斯須過盡，若不防者，必至危斃。

translations.literal: The wind races swiftly and passes in an instant; if one does not guard against it, one will surely come to deadly peril.
translations.idiomatic: The gale passes in moments; without precautions, death is certain.

sentences.zh: 于闐國，在且末西北，葱嶺之北二百餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Khotan lies northwest of Qiemo, more than two hundred li north of the Pamirs.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan lies northwest of Qiemo, two hundred-odd li north of the Pamirs.

sentences.zh: 東去鄯善千五百里，南去女國二千里，[5]西去朱俱波千里，[6]北去龜茲千四百里，去代九千八百里。

translations.literal: East to Shanshan is one thousand five hundred li; south to the Women's Kingdom two thousand li; west to Zhujubo one thousand li; north to Kucha one thousand four hundred li; from Dai nine thousand eight hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: It is fifteen hundred li east of Shanshan, two thousand li south of the Women's Kingdom, a thousand li west of Zhujubo, fourteen hundred li north of Kucha, and ninety-eight hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其地方亘千里，連山相次。

translations.literal: Its territory extends a thousand li square; ranges of mountains succeed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Its domain spans a thousand li, with mountain chains running in succession.

sentences.zh: 所都城方八九里，部內有大城五，小城數十。

translations.literal: Its capital city is eight or nine li square; within the domain are five great cities and several tens of small cities.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measures eight or nine li on a side; within the realm are five major towns and dozens of lesser ones.

sentences.zh: 于闐城東三十里有首拔河，中出玉石。

translations.literal: Thirty li east of Khotan city is the Shouba River, which yields jade within it.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li east of Khotan runs the Shouba River, famed for its jade.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀并桑麻，山多美玉，有好馬、駝、騾。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains as well as mulberry and hemp; the mountains have much fine jade; there are good horses, camels, and mules.
translations.idiomatic: The land grows grain, mulberry, and hemp; its mountains yield fine jade; it breeds excellent horses, camels, and mules.

sentences.zh: 其刑法，殺人者死，餘罪各隨輕重懲罰之。

translations.literal: Their penal code: murderers are put to death; other crimes are each punished according to severity.
translations.idiomatic: Murder is punished by death; lesser offenses by penalties suited to their gravity.

sentences.zh: 自外風俗物產與龜茲略同。

translations.literal: Apart from this, customs and products are roughly the same as Kucha's.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise its customs and products resemble those of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 俗重佛法，寺塔僧尼甚眾，王尤信尚，每設齋日，必親自灑掃饋食焉。

translations.literal: The custom esteems the Buddhist Law; temples, stupas, monks, and nuns are very numerous; the king especially believes and honors it—on each fast-day assembly he personally sweeps, sprinkles, and offers food.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is deeply revered; monasteries, stupas, and clergy abound, and the king is a devoted patron who personally sweeps temples and offers food on fast days.

sentences.zh: 城南五十里有贊摩寺，即昔羅漢比丘盧旃為其王造覆盆浮圖之所，[7]石上有辟支佛跣處，雙跡猶存。

translations.literal: Fifty li south of the city is Zanmo Temple—the place where long ago the arhat monk Luzhan built an inverted-bowl stupa for its king; on the stone are the barefoot marks of a pratyekabuddha, and the paired traces still remain.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li south stands Zanmo Temple, where the arhat Luzhan once built a stupa for the king; on the rock are a pratyekabuddha's footprints, still visible in pairs.

sentences.zh: 于闐西五百里有比摩寺，[8]云是老子化胡成佛之所。

translations.literal: Five hundred li west of Khotan is Bimo Temple—it is said to be the place where Laozi transformed the barbarians and became a Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li west lies Bimo Temple, traditionally the site where Laozi converted the barbarians and attained Buddhahood.

sentences.zh: 俗無禮義，多盜賊，淫縱。

translations.literal: The custom lacks ritual and righteousness; there are many bandits and thieves, and licentious excess.
translations.idiomatic: Morals are loose, banditry common, and conduct often dissolute.

sentences.zh: 自高昌以西，諸國人等深目高鼻，唯此一國，貌不甚胡，頗類華夏。

translations.literal: From Gaochang westward, the people of the various states have deep eyes and high noses; only this one state does not look very barbarian and rather resembles Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: West of Gaochang the peoples have deep-set eyes and prominent noses; Khotan alone looks less foreign and more Chinese in appearance.

sentences.zh: 城東二十里有大水北流，號樹枝水，[9]即黃河也，一名計式水。

translations.literal: Twenty li east of the city is a great river flowing north, called the Branching Waters—it is the Yellow River, also named the Jishi River.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li east a great river flows north—the Branching Waters, identified with the Yellow River and also called the Jishi.

sentences.zh: 城西五十五里亦有大水，[10]名達利水，與樹枝水會，俱北流。

translations.literal: Fifty-five li west of the city is also a great river, named the Dali River; it joins the Branching Waters and both flow north.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-five li west is another great stream, the Dali, which meets the Branching Waters and flows north with it.

sentences.zh: 真君中，世祖詔高涼王那擊吐谷渾慕利延，慕利延懼，驅其部落渡流沙。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era, the Shizu Emperor ordered the Prince of Gaoliang, Na, to attack Murong Muliyan of Tuyuhun; Muliyan was afraid and drove his tribes across the shifting sands.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenjun, Emperor Taiwu sent Prince Na of Gaoliang against Tuyuhun's Muliyan, who fled with his tribes across the desert.

sentences.zh: 那進軍急追之，慕利延遂西入于闐，殺其王，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Na advanced his army in hot pursuit; Muliyan thereupon entered Khotan from the west, killed its king, and the dead were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Na pressed the pursuit; Muliyan drove west into Khotan, killed the king, and left many dead.

sentences.zh: 顯祖末，蠕蠕寇于闐，于闐患之，遣使素目伽上表曰：「西方諸國，今皆已屬蠕蠕，奴世奉大國，至今無異。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xianzu's reign, the Rouran raided Khotan; Khotan was troubled by this and sent the envoy Sumujia to memorialize: "The western states are now all subject to the Rouran; your servant has for generations served the great state and to this day is unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Xianwen's reign the Rouran attacked Khotan. The king sent Sumujia with a memorial: "The western states have all fallen to the Rouran, yet we have always served the great empire faithfully.

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕軍馬到城下，奴聚兵自固，故遣使奉獻，延望救援。」

translations.literal: Now the Rouran army and horses have reached below the walls; your servant has gathered troops to hold firm, and therefore sends envoys with tribute, looking far for rescue."
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran now besiege our walls. I have mustered our forces to defend the city and send this tribute in hope of aid."

sentences.zh: 顯祖詔公卿議之，公卿奏曰：「于闐去京師幾萬里，蠕蠕之性，惟習野掠，不能攻城，若為所拒，當已旋矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu ordered the high ministers to deliberate; they memorialized: "Khotan is tens of thousands of li from the capital; the nature of the Rouran is only accustomed to wild raiding—they cannot besiege cities; if they are resisted, they should already have turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen consulted his ministers, who replied: "Khotan lies many thousands of li away. The Rouran raid the open country but cannot take walled cities; if resisted, they will withdraw.

sentences.zh: 雖欲遣師，勢無所及。」

translations.literal: Even if we wished to send troops, the situation cannot reach there."
translations.idiomatic: Even if we wished to send an army, we could not reach them in time."

sentences.zh: 顯祖以公卿議示其使者，亦以為然。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu showed the high ministers' deliberation to their envoy, who also considered it so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed this reply to Khotan's envoy, who agreed it was true.

sentences.zh: 於是詔之曰：「朕承天理物，欲令萬方各安其所，應敕諸軍以拯汝難。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict to them: "We receive Heaven's principle and govern things, wishing to let the ten thousand regions each rest in their place—we ought to order the armies to save you from hardship.
translations.idiomatic: He then told them: "I govern by Heaven's mandate and wish all lands peace; I should order the armies to relieve your distress.

sentences.zh: 但去汝遐阻，雖復遣援，不救當時之急，已停師不行，汝宜知之。

translations.literal: But you are far and blocked; even if we again sent aid, it would not rescue the urgency of the moment—the troops have already been halted and will not march; you should know this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are too remote; reinforcements could not arrive in time. I have halted the march—you must understand.

sentences.zh: 朕今練甲養卒，一二歲間當躬率猛將，為汝除患，汝其謹警候以待大舉。」

translations.literal: We now drill armor and nurture soldiers; within one or two years We shall personally lead fierce generals to remove your affliction—you should carefully watch and wait for the great campaign."
translations.idiomatic: I am training troops now; within a year or two I shall lead my best generals in person to end your troubles. Stand ready for that day."

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷遣使者韓羊皮使波斯，波斯王遣使獻馴象及珍物。

translations.literal: Earlier, the court had sent the envoy Han Yangpi as envoy to Persia; the king of Persia sent envoys presenting tame elephants and precious objects.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had sent Han Yangpi to Persia; the Persian king returned envoys bearing tame elephants and rare goods.

sentences.zh: 經于闐，于闐中于王秋仁輒留之，[11]假言慮有寇不達。

translations.literal: Passing through Khotan, the acting king of Khotan, Qiuren, detained them, falsely saying he feared there were raiders and they could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Khotan, the regent Qiuren detained them, claiming bandits blocked the road.

sentences.zh: 羊皮言狀，顯祖怒，又遣羊皮奉詔責讓之，自後每使朝獻。

translations.literal: Yangpi reported the situation; Emperor Xianzu was angry and again sent Yangpi bearing an edict to reprove and blame them; from then on, on each mission they came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yangpi reported the affair; the emperor was furious and sent him back with a rebuke. Thereafter Khotan sent tribute with every embassy.

sentences.zh: 蒲山-悉居半-權於摩-渠莎

translations.literal: Pishan—Xijuban—Quyumo—Qusha.
translations.idiomatic: Pishan, Xijuban, Quyumo, Qusha (place-name entries).

sentences.zh: 蒲山國，故皮山國也。

translations.literal: The state of Pishan is the former state of Pishan (Pishan).
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Pishan is the old state of Pishan.

sentences.zh: 居皮城，在于闐南，去代一萬二千里。

translations.literal: It dwells at Pi City, south of Khotan, twelve thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Its seat is Pi city, south of Khotan, twelve thousand li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其國西南三里，有凍凌山。

translations.literal: Three li southwest of the state is Mount Dongling.
translations.idiomatic: Three li southwest of the kingdom lies Mount Dongling.

sentences.zh: 後役屬于闐。

translations.literal: Later it was subordinated and attached to Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: It later came under Khotan's control.

sentences.zh: 悉居半國，故西夜國也，一名子合。

translations.literal: The state of Xijuban is the former state of Xiye; its other name is Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Xijuban is the former Western Yarkand, also called Zihe.

sentences.zh: 其王號子，治呼犍。

translations.literal: Its king takes the title Zi and governs from Hujian.
translations.idiomatic: Its king bears the title Zi and rules from Hujian.

sentences.zh: [12]在于闐西，去代萬二千九百七十里。

translations.literal: [12] It lies west of Khotan, twelve thousand nine hundred seventy li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: [12] It lies west of Khotan, twelve thousand nine hundred seventy li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 太延初，遣使來獻，自後貢使不絕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiyan, they sent envoys to present tribute; from then on tribute missions did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taiyan era it sent the first envoys with tribute; embassies thereafter never stopped coming.

sentences.zh: 權於摩國，故烏秅國也。

translations.literal: The state of Quyumo is the former state of Wunuo.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Quyumo is the old state of Wunuo.

sentences.zh: 其王居烏秅城，在悉居半西南，去代一萬二千九百七十里。

translations.literal: Its king dwells at Wunuo City, southwest of Xijuban, twelve thousand nine hundred seventy li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Its king resides at Wunuo, southwest of Xijuban, twelve thousand nine hundred seventy li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 渠莎國，居故莎車城，在子合西北，去代一萬二千九百八十里。

translations.literal: The state of Qusha dwells at the former Shache city, northwest of Zihe, twelve thousand nine hundred eighty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Qusha occupies old Yarkand (Shache), northwest of Zihe, twelve thousand nine hundred eighty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 車師-且彌

translations.literal: Jushi—Qiemi.
translations.idiomatic: Jushi and Qiemi (section entries).

sentences.zh: 車師國，一名前部。

translations.literal: The state of Jushi, also called the Front Division.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Jushi, also known as the Front Division.

sentences.zh: 其王居交河城。

translations.literal: Its king dwells at Jiaohe City.
translations.idiomatic: Its king resides at Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 去代萬五十里，其地北接蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Ten thousand fifty li from Dai; its territory adjoins the Rouran to the north.
translations.idiomatic: It lies ten thousand fifty li from Dai; to the north it borders the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 本通使交易，世祖初，始遣使朝獻，詔行人王恩生、許綱等出使。

translations.literal: Formerly they exchanged envoys and traded; at the beginning of Shizu's reign they first sent envoys to court with tribute, and an edict ordered the traveling envoys Wang Ensheng, Xu Gang, and others to go as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: It had long traded through diplomatic contact; early in Emperor Taiwu's reign it first sent tribute missions, and the court dispatched the envoys Wang Ensheng and Xu Gang westward.

sentences.zh: 恩生等始度流沙，為蠕蠕所執。

translations.literal: Ensheng and the others had just crossed the shifting sands when they were seized by the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Ensheng's party had barely crossed the desert when the Rouran captured them.

sentences.zh: 恩生見蠕蠕吳提，持魏節不為之屈。

translations.literal: Ensheng saw the Rouran khan Wuti and, holding Wei's credentials of office, did not submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Brought before the Rouran khan Wuti, Ensheng kept his Wei credential staff and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 後世祖切讓吳提，吳提懼，乃遣恩生等歸。

translations.literal: Later the Shizu Emperor sharply rebuked Wuti; Wuti was afraid and thereupon sent Ensheng and the others back.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu eventually rebuked Wuti sharply; frightened, the khan released Ensheng's party.

sentences.zh: 許綱到敦煌，病死，朝廷壯其節，賜諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Xu Gang reached Dunhuang and died of illness; the court admired his steadfastness and granted the posthumous epithet Zhen (Steadfast).
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gang died of illness at Dunhuang; the court honored his loyalty with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 初，沮渠無諱兄弟之渡流沙也，鳩集遺人，破車師國。

translations.literal: At first, when Juqu Wuhui and his brothers crossed the shifting sands, they gathered scattered survivors and destroyed the state of Jushi.
translations.idiomatic: When Juqu Wuhui and his brothers crossed the desert, they mustered survivors and overran Jushi.

sentences.zh: 真君十一年，車師王車夷落遣使琢進、薛直上書曰：「臣亡父僻處塞外，仰慕天子威德，遣使表獻，不空於歲。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhenjun, the king of Jushi, Che Yiluo, sent the envoys Zhuojin and Xue Zhi to submit a memorial saying: "My late father, dwelling remote beyond the frontier, admired the Son of Heaven's authority and virtue and sent envoys to present tribute—no year was left empty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhenjun, King Che Yiluo of Jushi sent Zhuojin and Xue Zhi with a memorial: "My late father, living beyond the frontier, revered the emperor's majesty and sent tribute every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 天子降念，賜遺甚厚。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven lowered his concern and bestowed gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in his kindness sent lavish gifts in return.

sentences.zh: 及臣繼立，亦不闕常貢，天子垂矜，亦不異前世。

translations.literal: When your servant succeeded to the throne, regular tribute was not lacking either; the Son of Heaven showed compassionate favor no different from former generations.
translations.idiomatic: When I succeeded him, I too kept up regular tribute, and the emperor's gracious treatment has been no less than before.

sentences.zh: 敢緣至恩，輒陳私艱。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures, owing to this utmost grace, to set forth private hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Presuming on your boundless grace, I beg leave to speak of my own distress.

sentences.zh: 臣國自無諱所攻擊，經今八歲，人民饑荒，無以存活。

translations.literal: Since your servant's state was attacked by Wuhui, eight years have passed; the people suffer famine and have no means to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhui's assaults have continued for eight years; famine has left my people with no means to live.

sentences.zh: 賊今攻臣甚急，臣不能自全，遂捨國東奔，三分免一，即日已到焉耆東界。

translations.literal: The bandits now press the attack very urgently; your servant cannot preserve himself and therefore abandoned the state and fled east—only one in three escaped; on that very day they had already reached the eastern border of Karasahr.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy presses hard; unable to hold my kingdom, I fled east with only a third of my people—and we have already reached Karasahr's eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 思歸天闕，幸垂賑救。」

translations.literal: Thinking of returning to the Heavenly Palace, may you mercifully extend relief and rescue."
translations.idiomatic: Longing to return to your court, I pray you will grant us relief.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔撫慰之，開焉耆倉給之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to comfort and reassure them, and Karasahr's granaries were opened to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict of consolation and ordered Karasahr's granaries opened to feed them.

sentences.zh: 正平初，遣子入侍，自後每使朝貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengping, he sent his son to attend at court; from then on, on each mission they came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhengping era he sent his son as hostage; thereafter tribute came with every embassy.

sentences.zh: 且彌國，都天山東于大谷，在車師北，去代一萬五百七十里。

translations.literal: The state of Qiemi has its capital at East Yudagu in the Tianshan, north of Jushi, ten thousand five hundred seventy li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Qiemi has its seat at East Yudagu in the Tianshan range, north of Jushi, ten thousand five hundred seventy li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 本役屬車師。

translations.literal: Originally it was subordinated and attached to Jushi.
translations.idiomatic: It originally came under Jushi's authority.

sentences.zh: 焉耆國，在車師南，都員渠城，白山南七十里，漢時舊國也。

translations.literal: The state of Karasahr lies south of Jushi; its capital is Yuanqu City, seventy li south of White Mountain—it is a former state from Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Karasahr lies south of Jushi, with its capital at Yuanqu seventy li south of White Mountain; it is an ancient kingdom dating to Han times.

sentences.zh: 去代一萬二百里。

translations.literal: Ten thousand two hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It is ten thousand two hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其王姓龍，名鳩尸卑那，即前涼張軌所討龍熙之胤。

translations.literal: Its king bears the surname Long and the name Jiushibina—he is a descendant of Long Xi whom Zhang Gui of Former Liang attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The king, surnamed Long and named Jiushibina, is a descendant of Long Xi, whom Zhang Gui of Former Liang had subjugated.

sentences.zh: 所都城方二里，國內凡有九城。

translations.literal: Its capital city is two li square; within the state there are nine cities in all.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is two li square, and the realm contains nine walled towns in all.

sentences.zh: 國小人貧，無綱紀法令。

translations.literal: The state is small and the people poor; there are no statutes or laws.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom is small and poor, with little organized government.

sentences.zh: 兵有弓刀甲矟。

translations.literal: Their arms include bows, swords, armor, and spears.
translations.idiomatic: Their soldiers carry bows, swords, armor, and spears.

sentences.zh: 婚姻略同華夏。

translations.literal: Marriage customs are roughly the same as Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage customs roughly follow Chinese practice.

sentences.zh: 死亡者皆焚而後葬，其服制滿七日則除之。

translations.literal: The dead are all cremated before burial; mourning garments are removed after a full seven days.
translations.idiomatic: The dead are cremated before interment; mourning dress is laid aside after seven days.

sentences.zh: 丈夫並翦髮以為首飾。

translations.literal: Husbands all cut their hair short as head ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Men all crop their hair short as a head ornament.

sentences.zh: 文字與婆羅門同。

translations.literal: Their script is the same as Brahmin script.
translations.idiomatic: Their writing follows the Brahmi script.

sentences.zh: 俗事天神，並崇信佛法。

translations.literal: The custom serves Heaven spirits and also reveres and believes in the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: They worship heavenly deities and also honor Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 尤重二月八日、四月八日，是日也，其國咸依釋教，齋戒行道焉。

translations.literal: They especially esteem the eighth day of the second month and the eighth day of the fourth month; on those days the whole state follows the Buddhist teaching, fasting, observing precepts, and walking the path.
translations.idiomatic: They especially observe the eighth days of the second and fourth months, when the entire kingdom fasts and practices according to Buddhist rites.

sentences.zh: 氣候寒，土田良沃，穀有稻粟菽麥，畜有駝馬。

translations.literal: The climate is cold; the fields are fertile; grains include rice, millet, beans, and wheat; livestock include camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is cold but the soil rich; they grow rice, millet, beans, and wheat, and raise camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 養蠶不以為絲，唯充綿纊。

translations.literal: They raise silkworms but do not use them for thread—only to fill cotton padding.
translations.idiomatic: They raise silkworms not for silk thread but for cotton padding.

sentences.zh: 俗尚蒲萄酒，兼愛音樂。

translations.literal: The custom esteems grape wine and also loves music.
translations.idiomatic: They favor grape wine and delight in music.

sentences.zh: 南去海十餘里，有魚鹽蒲葦之饒。

translations.literal: A little more than ten li south is the sea; there is abundance of fish, salt, reeds, and rushes.
translations.idiomatic: A little over ten li to the south lies a lake rich in fish, salt, and reeds.

sentences.zh: 東去高昌九百里；

translations.literal: East to Gaochang is nine hundred li;
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang lies nine hundred li to the east;

sentences.zh: 西去龜茲九百里，皆沙磧；

translations.literal: west to Kucha is nine hundred li, all sandy desert;
translations.idiomatic: Kucha nine hundred li to the west, across sandy wastes;

sentences.zh: 東南去瓜州二千二百里。

translations.literal: southeast to Guazhou is two thousand two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Guazhou is two thousand two hundred li to the southeast.

sentences.zh: 恃地多險，頗剽劫中國使。

translations.literal: Relying on the land's many natural defenses, they rather plundered and robbed Chinese envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in their rugged terrain, they frequently raided Wei envoys.

sentences.zh: 世祖怒之，詔成周公萬度歸討之，約齎輕糧，取食路次。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor was angry and issued an edict the Duke of Cheng, Wan Dugui, to attack them, stipulating light provisions and taking food along the route.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu, enraged, ordered Wan Dugui, Duke of Cheng, to punish them, instructing him to travel light and live off the land.

sentences.zh: 度歸入焉耆東界，擊其邊守左回、尉犁二城拔之，進軍向員渠。

translations.literal: Dugui entered Karasahr's eastern border, struck and captured the frontier garrisons of Zuohui and Yuli, two cities taken, and advanced the army toward Yuanqu.
translations.idiomatic: Dugui crossed Karasahr's eastern frontier, stormed the border towns of Zuohui and Yuli, and marched on Yuanqu.

sentences.zh: 鳩尸卑那以四五萬人出城守險以拒。

translations.literal: Jiushibina came out of the city with forty or fifty thousand men to hold the defiles and resist.
translations.idiomatic: Jiushibina marched out with forty to fifty thousand men to hold the passes against him.

sentences.zh: 度歸募壯勇，短兵直往衝，鳩尸卑那眾大潰，盡虜之，單騎走入山中。

translations.literal: Dugui recruited stout warriors and with short weapons charged straight forward; Jiushibina's host broke and fled in great disorder—all were captured; he alone fled on horseback into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Dugui picked his bravest men for a close assault; Jiushibina's army collapsed, his troops were taken wholesale, and he alone galloped into the hills.

sentences.zh: 度歸進屠其城，四鄙諸戎皆降服。

translations.literal: Dugui advanced and slaughtered the city; all the various Rong of the four frontiers submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Dugui sacked the city; neighboring peoples submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 焉耆為國，斗絕一隅，不亂日久，獲其珍奇異玩殊方譎詭不識之物，橐駝馬牛雜畜巨萬。

translations.literal: Karasahr as a state was tucked in a remote corner and had been undisturbed for long; they seized its precious and strange curios, exotic rarities beyond recognition, and camels, horses, cattle, and mixed livestock by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Long isolated and untroubled, Karasahr yielded exotic treasures and tens of thousands of camels, horses, and cattle.

sentences.zh: 時世祖幸陰山北宮，度歸破焉耆露板至，世祖省訖，賜司徒崔浩書曰：「萬度歸以五千騎經萬餘里，拔焉耆三城，獲其珍奇異物及諸委積不可勝數。

translations.literal: At that time the Shizu Emperor was visiting the Northern Palace at Yinshan; when the victory report of Dugui's conquest of Karasahr arrived, the emperor read it through and wrote to Minister of Works Cui Hao: "Wan Dugui with five thousand horsemen traveled more than ten thousand li, captured three cities of Karasahr, and seized their precious and strange objects and all stored accumulations beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at the Yinshan Northern Palace when Dugui's victory dispatch arrived. After reading it, he wrote to Cui Hao: "Wan Dugui led five thousand horse twelve thousand li, took three Karasahr cities, and seized treasures and stores beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王雖云即序西戎，有如指注，不能控引也。

translations.literal: From antiquity emperors, though they say the Western Rong are brought into order, it is like pointing but cannot draw them in.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors since antiquity spoke of bringing the western peoples to order, but that was mere gesture—they could never truly command them.

sentences.zh: 朕今手把而有之，如何？」

translations.literal: We now hold them in our hand and possess them—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I hold them in my hand—what do you say to that?"

sentences.zh: 浩上書稱美，遂命度歸鎮撫其人。

translations.literal: Hao submitted a memorial praising this, and Dugui was thereupon ordered to garrison and pacify its people.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wrote back in praise, and the emperor ordered Dugui to garrison and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 初鳩尸卑那走山中，猶覬城不拔，得還其國。

translations.literal: At first, when Jiushibina fled into the mountains, he still hoped the city would not be taken and that he could return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiushibina fled to the hills, he still hoped the city might hold and he could return.

sentences.zh: 既見盡為度歸所克，乃奔龜茲，龜茲以其壻，厚待之。

translations.literal: When he saw that all had been overcome by Dugui, he then fled to Kucha; Kucha treated him generously as their son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Finding all lost to Dugui, he fled to Kucha, where as the king's son-in-law he was warmly received.

sentences.zh: 龜茲國，在尉犂西北，白山之南一百七十里，都延城，漢時舊國也。

translations.literal: The state of Kucha lies northwest of Yuli, one hundred seventy li south of White Mountain; its capital is Yancheng—it is a former state from Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha lies northwest of Yuli, one hundred seventy li south of White Mountain, with its capital at Yancheng; it is an ancient Han-era kingdom.

sentences.zh: 去代一萬二百八十里。

translations.literal: Ten thousand two hundred eighty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It is ten thousand two hundred eighty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其王姓白，即後涼呂光所立白震之後。

translations.literal: Its king bears the surname Bai—he is a descendant of Bai Zhen whom Lü Guang of Later Liang installed.
translations.idiomatic: The king, surnamed Bai, descends from Bai Zhen, whom Lü Guang of Later Liang had enthroned.

sentences.zh: 其王頭繫綵帶，垂之於後，坐金師子牀。

translations.literal: The king ties a colored sash on his head, letting it hang down behind, and sits on a golden lion couch.
translations.idiomatic: The king wears a colored sash trailing behind his head and sits on a golden lion throne.

sentences.zh: 所居城方五六里。

translations.literal: The city where he dwells is five or six li square.
translations.idiomatic: The royal city measures five or six li on a side.

sentences.zh: 其刑法，殺人者死，劫賊則斷其一臂并刖一足。

translations.literal: Their penal code: murderers are put to death; robbers have one arm cut off together with one foot amputated.
translations.idiomatic: Murder is punishable by death; robbery by severing one arm and one foot.

sentences.zh: 稅賦準地徵租，無田者則稅銀錢。

translations.literal: Taxes and levies collect rent according to land; those without fields are taxed in silver cash.
translations.idiomatic: Landholders pay rent by acre; the landless pay in silver coin.

sentences.zh: 風俗、婚姻、喪葬、物產與焉耆略同，唯氣候少溫為異。

translations.literal: Customs, marriage, funerals, and products are roughly the same as Karasahr's; only the climate is slightly warmer as a difference.
translations.idiomatic: Customs, marriage, funerals, and produce resemble Karasahr's, except that the climate is somewhat warmer.

sentences.zh: 又出細氈，饒銅、鐵、鉛、麖皮、氍毹、鐃沙、[13]鹽綠、雌黃、胡粉、安息香、良馬、犎牛等。

translations.literal: It also produces fine felt; it is rich in copper, iron, lead, musk-deer hide, carpets, bell sand, [13] salt-green, orpiment, lead white, benzoin, fine horses, zebu cattle, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: It also exports fine felt and is rich in copper, iron, lead, musk-deer hide, carpets, bell sand, [13] salt-green, orpiment, lead white, benzoin, fine horses, and zebu cattle.

sentences.zh: 東有輪臺，即漢貳師將軍李廣利所屠者。

translations.literal: To the east is Luntai—the place the Han General of the Expediting Force, Li Guangli, slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Luntai lies to the east—the town Li Guangli of Han had destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其南三百里有大河東流，號計式水，即黃河也。

translations.literal: Three hundred li south is a great river flowing east, called the Jishi River—it is the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li to the south a great river runs east—the Jishi River, a branch of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 東去焉耆九百里，南去于闐一千四百里，西去疏勒一千五百里，北去突厥牙帳六百餘里，東南去瓜州三千一百里。

translations.literal: East to Karasahr nine hundred li; south to Khotan one thousand four hundred li; west to Kashgar one thousand five hundred li; north to the Turkish khan's yurt six hundred-odd li; southeast to Guazhou three thousand one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Karasahr is nine hundred li east, Khotan fourteen hundred li south, Kashgar fifteen hundred li west, the Turkish khan's camp six hundred-odd li north, and Guazhou thirty-one hundred li southeast.

translations.literal: [14] To its east
translations.idiomatic: [14] To its east

translations.literal: 〈Missing text〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Text missing.〉

sentences.zh: 城戍。

translations.literal: are fortified garrison towns.
translations.idiomatic: Stand fortified garrison towns.

sentences.zh: [15]寇竊非一。

translations.literal: [15] Raids and theft have occurred more than once.
translations.idiomatic: [15] They had raided repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔萬度歸率騎一千以擊之，龜茲遣烏羯目提等領兵三千距戰，度歸擊走之，斬二百餘級，大獲駝馬而還。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor ordered Wan Dugui to lead one thousand horsemen to attack them; Kucha dispatched Wujiemuti and others leading three thousand troops to resist in battle; Dugui struck and drove them off, beheading more than two hundred, and returned having seized great numbers of camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu sent Wan Dugui with a thousand horse; Kucha sent Wujiemuti with three thousand to meet him. Dugui routed them, took more than two hundred heads, and returned laden with camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 俗性多淫，置女巿，收男子錢入官。

translations.literal: The custom by nature is much licentious; they set up women's markets and collect men's money for the government.
translations.idiomatic: Prostitution was widespread; licensed brothels paid their fees to the state.

sentences.zh: 土多孔雀，羣飛山谷間，人取養而食之，孳乳如鷄鶩，其王家恒有千餘隻云。

translations.literal: The land has many peacocks; they fly in flocks among valleys; people catch and raise them for food, breeding them like chickens and ducks; it is said the royal house constantly has more than a thousand birds.
translations.idiomatic: Peacocks swarm the valleys; people raise them for food as easily as chickens, and the royal household reputedly keeps over a thousand.

sentences.zh: 其國西北大山中有如膏者流出成川，行數里入地，如䬾餬，甚臭，服之髮齒已落者能令更生，病人服之皆愈。

translations.literal: In the great mountains northwest of the state something like ointment flows out forming a stream; after going several li it sinks into the ground; it is like moist paste, very foul-smelling; those whose hair and teeth have already fallen, if they take it, can have them grow again; sick people who take it all recover.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest in the mountains a greasy substance flows out in a stream that sinks underground after a few li. Foul as moist paste, it restores hair and teeth once lost, and cures the sick who drink it.

sentences.zh: 自後每使朝貢。

translations.literal: From then on, on each mission they came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter it sent tribute with every embassy.

sentences.zh: 姑默國，居南城，在龜茲西，去代一萬五百里。

translations.literal: The state of Gumo dwells at South City, west of Kucha, ten thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Gumo occupies South City, west of Kucha, ten thousand five hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 役屬龜茲。

translations.literal: It is subordinated and attached to Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: It is subject to Kucha.

sentences.zh: 溫宿國，居溫宿城，在姑默西北，去代一萬五百五十里。

translations.literal: The state of Wensu dwells at Wensu City, northwest of Gumo, ten thousand five hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wensu has its seat at Wensu, northwest of Gumo, ten thousand five hundred fifty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 役屬龜茲。

translations.literal: It is subordinated and attached to Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: It is subject to Kucha.

sentences.zh: 尉頭國，居尉頭城，在溫宿北，去代一萬六百五十里。

translations.literal: The state of Weitou dwells at Weitou City, north of Wensu, ten thousand six hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Weitou occupies Weitou, north of Wensu, ten thousand six hundred fifty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 役屬龜茲。

translations.literal: It is subordinated and attached to Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: It is subject to Kucha.

sentences.zh: 烏孫-疏勒-悅般

translations.literal: Wusun—Kashgar—Yueban.
translations.idiomatic: Wusun, Kashgar, and Yueban (section entries).

sentences.zh: 烏孫國，居赤谷城，在龜茲西北，去代一萬八百里。

translations.literal: The state of Wusun dwells at Chigu City, northwest of Kucha, ten thousand eight hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wusun has its capital at Chigu, northwest of Kucha, ten thousand eight hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其國數為蠕蠕所侵，西徙葱嶺山中，無城郭，隨畜牧逐水草。

translations.literal: Its state has repeatedly been invaded by the Rouran; it migrated west into the Pamir mountains, without walled cities, following livestock and chasing water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated Rouran raids drove them west into the Pamirs; they have no fixed cities and follow their herds to pasture.

sentences.zh: 太延三年遣使者董琬等使其國，後每使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiyan, envoys including Dong Wan were dispatched to their state; later, on each mission they came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyan 3 the court sent Dong Wan and others there; tribute missions followed thereafter.

sentences.zh: 疏勒國，在姑默西，白山南百餘里，漢時舊國也。

translations.literal: The state of Kashgar lies west of Gumo, more than one hundred li south of White Mountain—it is a former state from Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar lies west of Gumo, a hundred-odd li south of White Mountain; it dates to Han times.

sentences.zh: 去代一萬一千二百五十里。

translations.literal: Eleven thousand two hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It is eleven thousand two hundred fifty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，其王遣使送釋迦牟尼佛袈裟一，長二丈餘。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign, its king sent envoys presenting one kāṣāya robe of Śākyamuni Buddha, more than two zhang in length.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign, its king sent envoys bearing a kāṣāya of Śākyamuni Buddha over two zhang long.

sentences.zh: 高宗以審是佛衣，應有靈異，遂燒之以驗虛實，置於猛火之上，經日不然，觀者莫不悚駭，心形俱肅。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, believing it truly to be the Buddha's robe and that it ought to have spiritual marvels, thereupon burned it to test truth and falsehood; placed upon fierce fire, after a full day it did not catch flame; none of the onlookers failed to be awestruck, hearts and bearing all solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced it was the Buddha's own robe and must hold miraculous power, Emperor Gaozong tested it in fierce fire—it would not burn for a full day. Witnesses were awestruck into reverent silence.

sentences.zh: 其王戴金師子冠。

translations.literal: Its king wears a golden lion crown.
translations.idiomatic: Its king wears a golden lion crown.

sentences.zh: 土多稻、粟、麻、麥、銅、鐵、錫、雌黃、錦、綿，每歲常供送於突厥。

translations.literal: The soil produces much rice, millet, hemp, wheat, copper, iron, tin, orpiment, brocade, and cotton floss; each year they regularly supply and deliver them to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The land yields rice, millet, hemp, wheat, copper, iron, tin, orpiment, brocade, and cotton floss, which it sends annually to the Turks as tribute.

sentences.zh: 其都城方五里，國內有大城十二，小城數十。

translations.literal: Its capital city is five li square; within the state there are twelve great cities and several tens of small cities.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is five li square, with twelve major towns and dozens of lesser ones across the realm.

sentences.zh: 人手足皆六指，產子非六指者即不育。

translations.literal: People's hands and feet all have six fingers; if a child born is not six-fingered, it will not be reared.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone has six fingers on hands and feet; infants born without six fingers are not raised.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二千人。

translations.literal: Fit troops: two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field two thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 南有黃河，西帶葱嶺，東去龜茲千五百里，西去鏺汗國千里，南去朱俱波八九百里，東北至突厥牙帳千餘里，東南去瓜州四千六百里。

translations.literal: South lies the Yellow River; west it borders the Pamirs; east to Kucha is one thousand five hundred li; west to the state of Bohann is one thousand li; south to Zhujubo eight or nine hundred li; northeast to the Turkish khan's yurt one thousand-odd li; southeast to Guazhou four thousand six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River lies to the south and the Pamirs belt the west; Kucha is fifteen hundred li east, Bohann a thousand li west, Zhujubo eight or nine hundred li south, the Turkish khan's camp a thousand-odd li northeast, and Guazhou forty-six hundred li southeast.

sentences.zh: 悅般國，在烏孫西北，去代一萬九百三十里。

translations.literal: The state of Yueban lies northwest of Wusun, ten thousand nine hundred thirty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yueban lies northwest of Wusun, ten thousand nine hundred thirty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其先，匈奴北單于之部落也。

translations.literal: In origin, it was a tribe of the Northern Chanyu of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: It descended from a tribe of the Xiongnu Northern Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 為漢車騎將軍竇憲所逐，北單于度金微山，西走康居，其羸弱不能去者住龜茲北。

translations.literal: Driven by Han General of Chariots and Cavalry Dou Xian, the Northern Chanyu crossed Mount Jinwei and fled west to Kangju; those too weak to go on remained north of Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: When Han General Dou Xian drove them out, the Northern Chanyu crossed Mount Jinwei and fled west to Kangju; the weak who could not keep up settled north of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 地方數千里，眾可二十餘萬。

translations.literal: The territory extends several thousand li; the population numbers roughly two hundred thousand-plus.
translations.idiomatic: Its domain spans thousands of li with a population of some two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 涼州人猶謂之「單于王」。

translations.literal: People of Liang Province still call them the "Chanyu King."
translations.idiomatic: People in Liang Province still refer to its ruler as the "Chanyu King."

sentences.zh: 其風俗言語與高車同，而其人清潔於胡。

translations.literal: Its customs and language are the same as the Gaoche, yet its people are cleaner than other barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs and speech match the Gaoche, but its people are more fastidious than other steppe peoples.

sentences.zh: 俗剪髮齊眉，以醍醐塗之，昱昱然光澤，日三澡漱，然後飲食。

translations.literal: The custom is to cut the hair level with the eyebrows, smear it with ghee until it gleams bright and lustrous, bathe and rinse three times daily, and only then eat and drink.
translations.idiomatic: They crop their hair to the brows and coat it with ghee until it shines; they wash three times a day before every meal.

sentences.zh: 其國南界有火山，山傍石皆燋鎔，流地數十里乃凝堅，人取為藥，即石流黃也。

translations.literal: On the southern border of their state is a fire mountain; the rocks beside it are all charred and melted, flowing over the ground for several tens of li before hardening; people take it for medicine—it is mineral sulfur.
translations.idiomatic: A volcano marks their southern frontier; its rocks melt and flow for dozens of li before hardening. People gather it as medicine—native sulfur.

sentences.zh: 與蠕蠕結好，其王嘗將數千人入蠕蠕國，欲與大檀相見。

translations.literal: Having sealed friendship with the Rouran, their king once led several thousand men into Rouran territory wishing to meet Datan.
translations.idiomatic: Allied with the Rouran, their king once marched several thousand men into Rouran lands to meet Khan Datan.

sentences.zh: 入其界百餘里，見其部人不浣衣，不絆髮，不洗手，婦人舌舐器物，王謂其從臣曰：「汝曹誑我入此狗國中！」

translations.literal: After entering their borders more than one hundred li, he saw their tribesmen not washing clothes, not binding hair, not washing hands, and women licking vessels with their tongues; the king said to his attendants: "You people deceived me into entering this dog country!
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li inside the border he found people who never washed clothes or hair or hands, and women who licked their dishes clean. The king told his followers: "You tricked me into this dog of a kingdom!

sentences.zh: 乃馳還。

translations.literal: With that he galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: He wheeled around and galloped home.

sentences.zh: 大檀遣騎追之不及，自是相仇讎，數相征討。

translations.literal: Datan dispatched horsemen in pursuit but could not overtake him; from then on they were mutual enemies and repeatedly sent expeditions against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Datan sent riders after him but failed to catch up; thereafter the two became bitter foes and raided each other repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 真君九年，遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenjun, they sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenjun (448), they sent tribute envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 并送幻人，稱能割人喉脉令斷，擊人頭令骨陷，皆血出或數升或盈斗，以草藥內其口中，令嚼咽之，須臾血止，養瘡一月復常，又無痕瘢。

translations.literal: They also sent illusionists who claimed they could cut a person's throat artery and sever it, strike a person's head and sink the bone—blood would flow in several sheng or fill a dou; placing herbal medicine in the mouth and having them chew and swallow, in a moment the blood stopped; nursing the wound one month restored normalcy, without scar or mark.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent wonder-workers who could slash throats or crush skulls until blood ran by the pitcher; a chewed herbal remedy stopped the bleeding at once, and within a month wounds healed without a scar.

sentences.zh: 世祖疑其虛，乃取死罪囚試之，皆驗。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor suspected it was a sham, so he took condemned prisoners to test it—all proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu, doubting the claim, tested them on condemned prisoners—every demonstration worked.

sentences.zh: 云中國諸名山皆有此草，乃使人受其術而厚遇之。

translations.literal: All famous mountains in Yunzhong have this herb; he thereupon had men receive their techniques and treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: The herb also grew on famed mountains in Yunzhong; the emperor had men learn their methods and rewarded them richly.

sentences.zh: 又言其國有大術者，蠕蠕來抄掠，術人能作霖雨狂風大雪及行潦，蠕蠕凍死漂亡者十二三。

translations.literal: They further said that in their state there was a great adept; when the Rouran came raiding, the adept could produce torrential rain, fierce wind, heavy snow, and running floodwaters—the Rouran who froze to death or were washed away numbered two or three out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: They also claimed a master in their land summoned torrential rains, gales, blizzards, and floods when the Rouran raided—killing or drowning two or three in ten.

sentences.zh: 是歲再遣使朝貢，求與官軍東西齊契討蠕蠕。

translations.literal: That year they again sent envoys with tribute, requesting to join with the imperial armies in east-west coordinated pact to attack the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: That year they sent tribute again, asking to coordinate with imperial forces east and west for a joint campaign against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉其意，命中外諸軍戒嚴，以淮南王他為前鋒，襲蠕蠕。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor approved their intent and ordered armies within and without to stand at alert; taking Prince Huainan Ta as vanguard, he raided the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu welcomed the proposal, put all armies on alert, and sent Prince Huainan Ta as vanguard in a raid on the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 仍詔有司以其鼓舞之節施於樂府。

translations.literal: He further ordered the responsible offices to apply their drum-and-dance rhythms to the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He also had their drum-and-dance music added to the court repertoire.

sentences.zh: 自後每使貢獻。

translations.literal: Afterward, on each mission they came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute with every embassy.

sentences.zh: 者至拔國，都者至拔城，在疏勒西，去代一萬一千六百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Zhezhiba—capital Zhezhiba City—lies west of Kashgar, eleven thousand six hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezhiba, capital Zhezhiba city, lies west of Kashgar, eleven thousand six hundred twenty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其國東有潘賀那山，出美鐵及師子。

translations.literal: East of their state is Mount Panhena, which produces fine iron and lions.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Panhena east of the realm yields fine iron and lions.

sentences.zh: 迷密國，都迷密城，在者至拔西，去代一萬二千六百里。

translations.literal: The state of Mimi—capital Mimi City—lies west of Zhezhiba, twelve thousand six hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Mimi, seat at Mimi city, lies west of Zhezhiba, twelve thousand six hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 正平元年，遣使獻一峯黑橐駝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengping, they sent envoys presenting one single-hump black camel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengping (554), they sent a single-hump black camel as tribute.

sentences.zh: 其國東有山，名郁悉滿，山出金玉，亦多鐵。

translations.literal: East of their state is a mountain named Yuximan; the mountain yields gold and jade, and iron is also abundant.
translations.idiomatic: East lies Mount Yuximan, rich in gold, jade, and iron.

sentences.zh: 悉萬斤國，都悉萬斤城，在迷密西，[16]去代一萬二千七百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Samarkand—capital Samarkand City—lies west of Mimi, [16] twelve thousand seven hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Samarkand, capital Samarkand city, lies west of Mimi, [16] twelve thousand seven hundred twenty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其國南有山，名伽色那，山出師子。

translations.literal: South of their state is a mountain named Gashna; the mountain produces lions.
translations.idiomatic: South stands Mount Gashna, home to lions.

sentences.zh: 每使朝貢。

translations.literal: On each mission they came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute with every embassy.

sentences.zh: 忸密國，都忸密城，在悉萬斤西，去代二萬二千八百二十八里。

translations.literal: The state of Wumi—capital Wumi City—lies west of Samarkand, twenty-two thousand eight hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wumi, capital Wumi city, lies west of Samarkand, twenty-two thousand eight hundred twenty-eight li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 洛那國，[17]故大宛國也。

translations.literal: The state of Luona, [17] the former state of Dayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Luona, [17] formerly the kingdom of Dayuan (Ferghana).

sentences.zh: 都貴山城，在疏勒西北，去代萬四千四百五十里。

translations.literal: Capital: Guishan City, northwest of Kashgar, fourteen thousand four hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital is Guishan city, northwest of Kashgar, fourteen thousand four hundred fifty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，遣使獻汗血馬，[18]自此每使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, they sent envoys presenting sweat-blood horses; [18] from then on on each mission they came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe (479), they sent Ferghana "blood-sweating" horses; [18] thereafter they tribute with every embassy.

sentences.zh: 粟特國，在葱嶺之西，古之奄蔡，一名溫那沙。

translations.literal: The state of Sogdiana lies west of the Pamirs—ancient Yancai—also called Wennasha.
translations.idiomatic: Sogdiana lies west of the Pamirs; it is ancient Yancai (Alans), also known as Wennasha.

sentences.zh: 居於大澤，在康居西北，去代一萬六千里。

translations.literal: It dwells beside a great marsh, northwest of Kangju, sixteen thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It sits by a great lake northwest of Kangju, sixteen thousand li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，匈奴殺其王而有其國，至王忽倪已三世矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Xiongnu killed its king and possessed its state; down to King Hunige, this has already been three generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu had killed its king and seized the realm; King Hunige was already the third generation since.

sentences.zh: 其國商人先多詣涼土販貨，及克姑臧，悉見虜。

translations.literal: Merchants of their state had previously often gone to Liang territory to trade goods; when Guchang was taken, all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Its merchants had long traded in Liangzhou; when Guchang fell, they were all taken captive.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，粟特王遣使請贖之，詔聽焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign, the king of Sogdiana sent envoys requesting to ransom them; an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozong's reign the Sogdian king sent envoys to ransom them, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 自後無使朝獻。

translations.literal: Afterward there were no envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no further tribute missions came.

sentences.zh: 波斯國，都宿利城，在忸密西，古條支國也。

translations.literal: The state of Persia—capital Suli City—lies west of Wumi; it is the ancient state of Tiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Persia, capital at Suli city, lies west of Wumi; this is ancient Tiaozhi (Parthia/Persis).

sentences.zh: 去代二萬四千二百二十八里。

translations.literal: Twenty-four thousand two hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It is twenty-four thousand two hundred twenty-eight li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 城方十里，戶十餘萬，河經其城中南流。

translations.literal: The city is ten li square, with households exceeding one hundred thousand; a river runs through the city flowing south.
translations.idiomatic: The capital spans ten li square with more than a hundred thousand households; a river runs south through its center.

sentences.zh: 土地平正，出金、銀、鍮石、珊瑚、琥珀、車渠、馬腦，多大真珠、頗梨、瑠璃、水精、瑟瑟、金剛、火齊、鑌鐵、銅、錫、朱砂、水銀、綾、錦、疊、毼、氍毹、毾㲪、赤麞皮，[19]及薰陸、鬱金、蘇合、青木等香，胡椒、畢撥、石蜜、千年棗、香附子、訶梨勒、無食子、鹽綠、雌黃等物。

translations.literal: The land is level and flat, producing gold, silver, orpiment-stone, coral, amber, carnelian, agate, and much genuine pearl, spinel, glass, crystal, lapis lazuli, diamond, pyrite, wrought iron, copper, tin, cinnabar, quicksilver, gauze, brocade, layered silks, felt, patterned rugs, carpets, red antelope hide, [19] and such fragrances as storax, turmeric, styrax, eaglewood, along with pepper, long pepper, rock sugar, millennium jujubes, cypress root, chebulic myrobalan, gallnuts, salt-green, and orpiment, among other goods.
translations.idiomatic: The land is flat and rich: gold, silver, coral, amber, carnelian, agate, pearls, lapis lazuli, diamonds, iron, copper, and tin; fine gauzes, brocades, felts, and rugs; aromatics from storax and eaglewood to pepper and rock sugar; medicinal plants and dyes galore. [19]

sentences.zh: 氣候暑熱，家自藏冰。

translations.literal: The climate is hot and sweltering; each household stores ice on its own.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is sweltering; families keep ice in store.

sentences.zh: 地多沙磧，引水溉灌。

translations.literal: The land has much sand and gravel desert; water is drawn for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the land is sandy desert, irrigated by canal.

sentences.zh: 其五穀及鳥獸等與中夏略同，唯無稻及黍、稷。

translations.literal: Its grains and birds and beasts are roughly the same as the Central Realm, except it lacks rice, broomcorn millet, and foxtail millet.
translations.idiomatic: Crops and fauna resemble China's, though rice, sorghum, and millet are absent.

sentences.zh: 土出名馬、大驢及駝，往往有日行七百里者。

translations.literal: The soil produces famed horses, large donkeys, and camels; often some can travel seven hundred li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: The land breeds renowned horses, great donkeys, and camels—some said to cover seven hundred li in a day.

sentences.zh: 富室至有數千頭。

translations.literal: Wealthy houses may have up to several thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households may own thousands of head.

sentences.zh: 又出白象、師子、大鳥卵。

translations.literal: It also produces white elephants, lions, and great bird eggs.
translations.idiomatic: White elephants, lions, and ostrich eggs are also found here.

sentences.zh: 有鳥形如橐駝，有兩翼，飛而不能高，食草與肉，亦能噉火。

translations.literal: There is a bird shaped like a camel, with two wings; it flies but cannot fly high, eats grass and meat, and can also devour fire.
translations.idiomatic: A camel-shaped bird with wings flies low, eats plants and flesh, and—remarkably—can consume fire.

sentences.zh: 其王姓波氏，名斯。
