translations.literal: Its king bears the surname Bo and the personal name Si.
translations.idiomatic: The king, surnamed Bo, is named Si (Peroz).

sentences.zh: 坐金羊牀，戴金花冠，衣錦袍、織成帔，飾以真珠寶物。

translations.literal: He sits on a golden sheep couch, wears a golden flower crown, robes of brocade and woven mantles, adorned with pearls and precious objects.
translations.idiomatic: He sits on a gilded couch, wears a gold floral crown, brocade robes and woven mantles studded with pearls and gems.

sentences.zh: 其俗丈夫剪髮，戴白皮帽，貫頭衫，兩厢近下開之，亦有巾帔，緣以織成；

translations.literal: Their custom: husbands cut their hair, wear white leather caps, head-piercing tunics split open low on both sides; they also have kerchiefs and mantles bordered with woven patterns;
translations.idiomatic: Men cut their hair short and wear white felt caps and tunics that slip over the head, split low on both sides; some add scarves and mantles with woven borders;

sentences.zh: 婦女服大衫，披大帔，其髮前為髻，後披之，飾以金銀花，仍貫五色珠，絡之於膊。

translations.literal: Women wear large tunics, draping large mantles; their hair is arranged in a topknot in front and hangs down behind, adorned with gold and silver flowers, and strung with five-colored beads looped on the arms.
translations.idiomatic: Women wear long tunics and flowing mantles, hair piled in front and loose behind, decorated with gold and silver flowers and five-colored beads strung on the arms.

sentences.zh: 王於其國內，別有小牙十餘所，猶中國之離宮也。

translations.literal: Within his state the king has separately more than ten lesser courts—like detached palaces of the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: The king maintains a dozen or more minor courts across the realm, like China's detached palaces.

sentences.zh: 每年四月出遊處之，十月乃還。

translations.literal: Each year in the fourth month he goes out touring and stays there; in the tenth month he then returns.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he tours these residences from the fourth month and returns in the tenth.

sentences.zh: 王即位以後，擇諸子內賢者，密書其名，封之於庫，諸子及大臣皆莫之知也。

translations.literal: After the king takes the throne, he selects the worthy among his sons, secretly writes the name, seals it in the treasury—none of the sons or great ministers knows it.
translations.idiomatic: On accession the king secretly writes the name of his worthiest son, seals the document in the treasury, and tells no one—not even the princes or ministers.

sentences.zh: 王死，眾乃發書視之，其封內有名者，即立以為王，餘子出各就邊任，兄弟更不相見也。

translations.literal: When the king dies, the multitude then opens the document and looks; whoever is named in the seal is immediately enthroned as king; the remaining sons go out each to border posts, and brothers never see one another again.
translations.idiomatic: At the king's death the sealed name is read aloud; that prince becomes king while the others depart for frontier posts, never to see each other again.

sentences.zh: 國人號王曰「醫囋」，妃曰「防步率」，王之諸子曰「殺野」。

translations.literal: The people of the state call the king "Yizha," the consort "Fangbulü," and the king's sons "Shaye."
translations.idiomatic: Subjects call the king Yizha, the queen Fangbulü, and royal princes Shaye.

sentences.zh: 大官有摸胡壇，掌國內獄訟；

translations.literal: Among high officers is the Mohutan, who manages domestic prisons and lawsuits;
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Mohutan handles prisons and lawsuits;

sentences.zh: 泥忽汗，掌庫藏開禁；

translations.literal: Ni Huhan, who manages treasury stores and seals;
translations.idiomatic: Ni Huhan oversees the treasury and its seals;

sentences.zh: [20]地卑，[21]掌文書及眾務；

translations.literal: [20] Dibei, [21] who manages documents and various affairs;
translations.idiomatic: [20] Dibei [21] manages records and general administration;

sentences.zh: 次有遏羅訶地，掌王之內事；

translations.literal: Next is Eluhedi, who manages the king's inner affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Eluhedi manages the royal household;

sentences.zh: 薛波勃，掌四方兵馬。

translations.literal: Xuebobe, who commands troops and horses in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Xuebobe commands armies on every frontier.

sentences.zh: 其下皆有屬官，分統其事。

translations.literal: Below each are subordinate officers who divide and govern their affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Each office has subordinates overseeing its duties.

sentences.zh: 兵有甲矟圓排劍弩弓箭，戰兼乘象，百人隨之。

translations.literal: Their troops have armor, spears, round shields, swords, crossbows, and bows and arrows; in battle they also mount elephants, with a hundred men following each.
translations.idiomatic: Their forces carry armor, spears, round shields, swords, crossbows, and bows; in battle they also field war elephants, each attended by a hundred foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其刑法：重罪懸諸竿上，射殺之；

translations.literal: Their penal law: for heavy crimes, [the offender] is hung on a pole and shot to death;
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes: the condemned is hung from a pole and shot;

sentences.zh: 次則繫獄，新王立乃釋之；

translations.literal: Next grade is imprisonment in jail—released only when a new king is enthroned;
translations.idiomatic: Lesser felonies mean prison until a new king's accession;

sentences.zh: 輕罪則劓刖若髠，或剪半鬢，及繫牌於項，以為耻辱；

translations.literal: For light crimes, nose-cutting, foot-cutting, or head-shaving, or cutting half the temple hair, and hanging a placard on the neck as shame;
translations.idiomatic: Petty offenses bring mutilation, shaving, half-cropped hair, or a placard hung on the neck in disgrace;

sentences.zh: 犯強盜者，繫之終身；

translations.literal: Robbers are imprisoned for life;
translations.idiomatic: Robbers are jailed for life;

sentences.zh: 姦貴人妻者，男子流，婦人割其耳鼻。

translations.literal: Those who violate noblemen's wives—men are exiled, women have their ears and nose cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Adultery with a nobleman's wife: the man is exiled, the woman loses ears and nose.

sentences.zh: 賦稅則準地輸銀錢。

translations.literal: Taxes and levies are assessed by land and paid in silver coin.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes are assessed by land and paid in silver.

sentences.zh: 俗事火神、天神。

translations.literal: Their custom honors the Fire God and Heaven God.
translations.idiomatic: They worship the gods of fire and heaven.

sentences.zh: 文字與胡書異。

translations.literal: Their script differs from barbarian writing.
translations.idiomatic: Their script differs from steppe scripts.

sentences.zh: 多以姊妹為妻妾，自餘婚合，亦不擇尊卑，諸夷之中最為醜穢矣。

translations.literal: Most take sisters as wives and concubines; for other marriages they likewise do not choose by rank—the most foul and shameful among all the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Sister marriage is common; otherwise they observe no rank in wedlock—the most abhorred custom among western peoples.

sentences.zh: 百姓女年十歲以上有姿貌者，王收養之，有功勳人即以分賜。

translations.literal: Commoners' daughters from age ten upward who have fine appearance—the king takes them for rearing; men of merit are then given shares as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The king gathers comely girls over ten from common families and bestows them on men of merit.

sentences.zh: 死者多棄屍於山，一月著服。

translations.literal: For the dead, many abandon corpses on mountains; mourning dress is worn one month.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses are often left on mountains; mourners wear funeral garb for one month.

sentences.zh: 城外有人別居，唯知喪葬之事，號為不淨人，若入城巿，搖鈴自別。

translations.literal: Outside the city some people live separately, knowing only funeral affairs—they are called "defiled persons"; if they enter the city market, they ring a bell to distinguish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Outcasts who handle only funeral rites live apart outside the walls; entering the market, they announce themselves with a bell.

sentences.zh: 以六月為歲首，尤重七月七日、十二月一日，其日人庶以上各相命召，設會作樂，以極歡娛。

translations.literal: They take the sixth month as the year's start; they especially esteem the seventh month seventh day and the twelfth month first day—on those days commoners upward all summon one another by invitation, setting feasts and making music to the utmost revelry.
translations.idiomatic: Their year begins in the sixth month; the seventh day of the seventh month and first day of the twelfth are grand festivals when everyone feasts and makes merry.

sentences.zh: 又每年正月二十日，各祭其先死者。

translations.literal: Furthermore, each year on the twentieth day of the first month, each sacrifices to their departed ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day of the first month they honor their dead.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，其國遣使上書貢物，云：「大國天子，天之所生，願日出處常為漢中天子。

translations.literal: During the Shengui era, their state sent envoys with a written memorial and tribute goods, saying: "Great state's Son of Heaven, heaven-born—may the place where the sun rises always be the Son of Heaven of Han China.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengui the Persians sent tribute with a letter: "Great Son of Heaven, born of heaven—may the land where the sun rises forever belong to the Han emperor.

sentences.zh: 波斯國王居和多千萬敬拜。」

translations.literal: The king of Persia, Juheduo, bows in utmost reverence.
translations.idiomatic: King Juheduo of Persia pays deepest homage."

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉納之。

translations.literal: The court approved and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court welcomed the message.

sentences.zh: 自此每使朝獻。

translations.literal: From then on, on each mission they came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Persia sent tribute with every embassy thereafter.

sentences.zh: 伏盧尼國，都伏盧尼城，在波斯國北，去代二萬七千三百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Volini—capital Volini City—lies north of Persia, twenty-seven thousand three hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Volini, capital Volini city, lies north of Persia, twenty-seven thousand three hundred twenty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 累石為城。

translations.literal: They pile stones to make walls.
translations.idiomatic: Its walls are stacked stone.

sentences.zh: 東有大河南流，中有鳥，其形似人，亦有如橐駝、馬者，皆有翼，常居水中，出水便死。

translations.literal: East lies a great river flowing south; in it are birds shaped like humans, and also like camels and horses—all winged; they constantly dwell in the water and die if they leave it.
translations.idiomatic: A great river flows east; winged bird-creatures shaped like men, camels, or horses live in its water and perish if they emerge.

sentences.zh: 城北有云尼山，出銀、珊瑚、琥珀，多師子。

translations.literal: North of the city is Mount Yunni, producing silver, coral, and amber; lions are many.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Yunni north of the capital yields silver, coral, and amber, and many lions.

sentences.zh: 色知顯國，都色知顯城，在悉萬斤西北，去代一萬二千九百四十里，土平，多五果。

translations.literal: The state of Sezhixian—capital Sezhixian City—lies northwest of Samarkand, twelve thousand nine hundred forty li from Dai; the soil is level, with many of the five fruits.
translations.idiomatic: Sezhixian, northwest of Samarkand and twelve thousand nine hundred forty li from the Wei capital, has level land rich in orchard fruits.

sentences.zh: 伽色尼國，都伽色尼城，在悉萬斤南，去代一萬二千九百里。

translations.literal: The state of Ghazni—capital Ghazni City—lies south of Samarkand, twelve thousand nine hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Ghazni, capital Ghazni city, lies south of Samarkand, twelve thousand nine hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 土出赤鹽，多五果。

translations.literal: The soil produces red salt; the five fruits are many.
translations.idiomatic: It yields red salt and abundant orchard fruit.

sentences.zh: 薄知國，都薄知城，在伽色尼南，去代一萬三千三百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Bozhi—capital Bozhi City—lies south of Ghazni, thirteen thousand three hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi, south of Ghazni, lies thirteen thousand three hundred twenty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 多五果。

translations.literal: The five fruits are many.
translations.idiomatic: Orchard fruits abound.

sentences.zh: 牟知國，都牟知城，在忸密西南，去代二萬二千九百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Muzhi—capital Muzhi City—lies southwest of Wumi, twenty-two thousand nine hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi, southwest of Wumi, is twenty-two thousand nine hundred twenty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 土平，禽獸草木類中國。

translations.literal: The soil is level; birds, beasts, grasses, and trees resemble those of China.
translations.idiomatic: Level land; its fauna and flora resemble China's.

sentences.zh: 阿弗太汗國，都阿弗太汗城，在忸密西，去代二萬三千七百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Afutaihan—capital Afutaihan City—lies west of Wumi, twenty-three thousand seven hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Afutaihan, west of Wumi, lies twenty-three thousand seven hundred twenty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 土平，多五果。

translations.literal: The soil is level; the five fruits are many.
translations.idiomatic: Level land with abundant orchard fruit.

sentences.zh: 呼似密國，都呼似密城，在阿弗太汗西，去代二萬四千七百里。

translations.literal: The state of Husimi—capital Husimi City—lies west of Afutaihan, twenty-four thousand seven hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Husimi, capital at Husimi city, lies west of Afutaihan, twenty-four thousand seven hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 土平，出銀、琥珀，有師子，多五果。

translations.literal: The soil is level; it produces silver and amber; there are lions; the five fruits are many.
translations.idiomatic: Level land yields silver and amber; lions roam there, and orchard fruits abound.

sentences.zh: 諾色波羅國，都波羅城，在忸密南，去代二萬三千四百二十八里。

translations.literal: The state of Nosebolo—capital Bolo City—lies south of Wumi, twenty-three thousand four hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Nosebolo, seat at Bolo city, lies south of Wumi, twenty-three thousand four hundred twenty-eight li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 土平，宜稻麥，多五果。

translations.literal: The soil is level; it is suited to rice and wheat; the five fruits are many.
translations.idiomatic: Level land suited to rice and wheat, with abundant orchard fruit.

sentences.zh: 早伽至國，都早伽至城，在忸密西，去代二萬三千七百二十八里。

translations.literal: The state of Zaojiazhi—capital Zaojiazhi City—lies west of Wumi, twenty-three thousand seven hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zaojiazhi, capital at Zaojiazhi city, lies west of Wumi, twenty-three thousand seven hundred twenty-eight li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 土平，少田植，取稻麥於隣國，有五果。

translations.literal: The soil is level; field planting is little—they obtain rice and wheat from neighboring states; it has the five fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The land is level but fields are sparse; grain comes from neighboring states, though orchard fruit is available.

sentences.zh: 伽不單國，都伽不單城，在悉萬斤西北，去代一萬二千七百八十里。

translations.literal: The state of Gabudan—capital Gabudan City—lies northwest of Samarkand, twelve thousand seven hundred eighty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Gabudan, northwest of Samarkand, lies twelve thousand seven hundred eighty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 土平，宜稻麥，有五果。

translations.literal: The soil is level; it is suited to rice and wheat; it has the five fruits.
translations.idiomatic: Level land suited to rice and wheat, with orchard fruits.

sentences.zh: 者舌國，故康居國，在破洛那西北，去代一萬五千四百五十里。

translations.literal: The state of Zhe She—the former state of Kangju—lies northwest of Ferghana, fifteen thousand four hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe She, once the land of Kangju, lies northwest of Ferghana, fifteen thousand four hundred fifty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 太延三年，遣使朝貢，自是不絕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiyan, they sent envoys to court with tribute; from then on it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyan 3 they first sent tribute envoys; embassies never ceased thereafter.

sentences.zh: 伽倍國，故休密翕侯。

translations.literal: The state of Jiabei—the former Xiumi Xihou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiabei, formerly the domain of the Xiumi chieftain.

sentences.zh: 都和墨城，在莎車西，去代一萬三千里。

translations.literal: Its capital is Hemo City, west of Yarkand, thirteen thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Capital at Hemo city, west of Yarkand, thirteen thousand li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 人居山谷間。

translations.literal: People dwell among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Its people live in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 折薛莫孫國，故雙靡翕侯。

translations.literal: The state of Zhiexiemosun—the former Shuangmi Xihou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiexiemosun, formerly the domain of the Shuangmi chieftain.

sentences.zh: 都雙靡城，在伽倍西，去代一萬三千五百里。

translations.literal: Its capital is Shuangmi City, west of Jiabei, thirteen thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Seat at Shuangmi city, west of Jiabei, thirteen thousand five hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 人居山谷間。

translations.literal: People dwell among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Its people live in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 鉗敦國，故貴霜翕侯。

translations.literal: The state of Qiandun—the former Guishuang Xihou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandun, formerly the domain of the Guishuang chieftain.

sentences.zh: 都護澡城，在折薛莫孫西，去代一萬三千五百六十里。

translations.literal: Its capital is Huzao City, west of Zhiexiemosun, thirteen thousand five hundred sixty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Seat at Huzao city, west of Zhiexiemosun, thirteen thousand five hundred sixty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 人居山谷間。

translations.literal: People dwell among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Its people live in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 弗敵沙國，故肸頓翕侯。

translations.literal: The state of Fudisha—the former Xidun Xihou.
translations.idiomatic: Fudisha, formerly the domain of the Xidun chieftain.

sentences.zh: 都薄茅城，在鉗敦西，去代一萬三千六百六十里。

translations.literal: Its capital is Bomao City, west of Qiandun, thirteen thousand six hundred sixty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Seat at Bomao city, west of Qiandun, thirteen thousand six hundred sixty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 居山谷間。

translations.literal: It dwells among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: It lies in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 閻浮謁國，故高附翕侯。

translations.literal: The state of Yanfuye—the former Gaofu Xihou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfuye, formerly the domain of the Gaofu chieftain.

sentences.zh: 都高附城，在弗敵沙南，去代一萬三千七百六十里。

translations.literal: Its capital is Gaofu City, south of Fudisha, thirteen thousand seven hundred sixty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Seat at Gaofu city, south of Fudisha, thirteen thousand seven hundred sixty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 居山谷間。

translations.literal: It dwells among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: It lies in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 大月氏國，都盧監氏城，在弗敵沙西，去代一萬四千五百里。

translations.literal: The state of the Great Yuezhi—capital Lujianshi City—lies west of Fudisha, fourteen thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Yuezhi, capital at Lujianshi, lies west of Fudisha, fourteen thousand five hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 北與蠕蠕接，數為所侵，遂西徙都薄羅城，去弗敵沙二千一百里。

translations.literal: To the north it adjoins the Rouran; repeatedly invaded by them, it then moved west and shifted its capital to Boluo City, twenty-one hundred li from Fudisha.
translations.idiomatic: Bordering the Rouran to the north, it was repeatedly raided and eventually moved its capital west to Boluo—twenty-one hundred li from Fudisha.

sentences.zh: 其王寄多羅勇武，遂興師越大山，南侵北天竺，自乾陁羅以北五國盡役屬之。

translations.literal: Its king Jiduoluo was brave and martial; he then raised an army, crossed the great mountains, invaded North India to the south, and from Gandhara northward five states all were forced to submit as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Its king Jiduoluo, a fierce warrior, marched his armies over the mountains into northern India and reduced five kingdoms north of Gandhara to tributary status.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，其國人商販京師，自云能鑄石為五色瑠璃，於是採礦山中，於京師鑄之。

translations.literal: During the Shizu era, merchants of that state trading at the capital declared they could cast stone into five-colored glass; thereupon ore was gathered in the mountains and cast at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taiwu's reign, Yuezhi traders in the capital claimed they could smelt stone into colored glass; ore was mined and the work done in the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 既成，光澤乃美於西方來者。

translations.literal: When completed, the luster was indeed finer than that of goods coming from the West.
translations.idiomatic: The finished glass outshone imports from the western lands.

sentences.zh: 乃詔為行殿，容百餘人，光色映徹，觀者見之，莫不驚駭，以為神明所作。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon had it made into a traveling hall, holding more than a hundred persons; light and color shone through—viewers who saw it were all startled and awestruck, thinking it the work of spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a traveling pavilion built to hold over a hundred people; its radiance astonished all who saw it—they took it for divine craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 自此中國瑠璃遂賤，人不復珍之。

translations.literal: From then on glass in China became cheap; people no longer treasured it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter domestic glass grew commonplace and lost its rarity.

sentences.zh: 安息國，在葱嶺西，都蔚搜城。

translations.literal: The state of Parthia lies west of the Pamirs; its capital is Weisou City.
translations.idiomatic: Parthia, west of the Pamirs, has its capital at Weisou city.

sentences.zh: 北與康居，西與波斯相接，在大月氏西北，去代二萬一千五百里。

translations.literal: North it adjoins Kangju; west it adjoins Persia; it lies northwest of the Great Yuezhi, twenty-one thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It borders Kangju to the north and Persia to the west, lying northwest of the Great Yuezhi and twenty-one thousand five hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 大秦國，一名黎軒，都安都城。

translations.literal: The state of Daqin—also called Li Xuan—has its capital at Andu City.
translations.idiomatic: Daqin (Rome), also known as Li Xuan, has its capital at Antioch (Andu).

sentences.zh: 從條支西渡海曲一萬里，去代三萬九千四百里。

translations.literal: From Tiaozhi, crossing the sea's bend westward ten thousand li, it is thirty-nine thousand four hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand li west from Tiaozhi across the sea's curve; thirty-nine thousand four hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其海傍出，猶勃海也，而東西與勃海相望，蓋自然之理。

translations.literal: Its sea branches outward, like the Bohai Sea; yet east and west it faces the Bohai Sea across the distance—presumably nature's principle.
translations.idiomatic: Its sea branches off like the Bohai; yet it faces the eastern Bohai across the world—such is nature's symmetry, the text suggests.

sentences.zh: 地方六千里，居兩海之間。

translations.literal: Its territory is six thousand li square; it lies between two seas.
translations.idiomatic: Its realm spans six thousand li, set between two seas.

sentences.zh: 其地平正，人居星布。

translations.literal: Its land is level and flat; people's dwellings are scattered like stars.
translations.idiomatic: The land is flat; settlements are scattered like stars.

sentences.zh: 其王都城分為五城，各方五里，周六十里。

translations.literal: The king's capital city is divided into five cities, each side five li, circumference sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: The royal capital comprises five walled quarters, each five li square, sixty li around in total.

sentences.zh: 王居中城。

translations.literal: The king dwells in the central city.
translations.idiomatic: The king resides in the central quarter.

sentences.zh: 城置八臣以主四方，而王城亦置八臣，分主四城。

translations.literal: Each city has eight officials to govern the four directions; the king's city also has eight officials, each governing one of the four outer cities.
translations.idiomatic: Each quarter has eight ministers overseeing the four directions; the central city likewise has eight, each administering one outer quarter.

sentences.zh: 若謀國事及四方有不決者，則四城之臣集議王所，王自聽之，然後施行。

translations.literal: When deliberating state affairs or when the four directions have undecided matters, the officials of the four cities assemble to confer at the king's place; the king personally hears them, and only then are measures enacted.
translations.idiomatic: When state policy or regional disputes required judgment, ministers from all quarters met before the king; he heard their counsel personally before anything was done.

sentences.zh: 王三年一出觀風化，人有冤枉詣王訴訟者，當方之臣小則讓責，大則黜退，令其舉賢人以代之。

translations.literal: Every three years the king goes out once to observe customs; when people with grievances come to the king to plead lawsuits, the officials of the relevant quarter receive minor rebuke and blame, or major dismissal and removal, and are ordered to recommend worthy men to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Every third year the king toured his realm. Wronged subjects who brought suits to him could cost local officials a reprimand or outright dismissal, with orders to find worthy replacements.

sentences.zh: 其人端正長大，衣服車旗擬儀中國，故外域謂之大秦。

translations.literal: Its people are upright and tall; clothes, chariots, and banners imitate China's ritual forms—therefore outer lands call it Daqin.
translations.idiomatic: The people are tall and fine-featured; their dress, carriages, and banners echo Chinese court style—hence foreign lands call the realm Daqin, "Great China."

sentences.zh: 其土宜五穀桑麻，人務蠶田，多璆琳、琅玕、神龜、白馬朱鬣、明珠、夜光璧。

translations.literal: Its soil suits the five grains, mulberry, and hemp; people devote themselves to sericulture and fields; it has much fine jade, coral, divine tortoises, white horses with red manes, luminous pearls, and night-shining disks.
translations.idiomatic: Grain, mulberry, and hemp flourish; sericulture is the main livelihood. Treasures abound: fine jade, coral, sacred tortoises, white horses with crimson manes, luminous pearls, and night-shining jade disks.

sentences.zh: 東南通交趾，又水道通益州永昌，郡多出異物。

translations.literal: Southeast it connects with Jiaozhi; moreover waterways connect with Yongchang in Yizhou—many strange goods come from those commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast routes reach Jiaozhi; waterways also link Yizhou's Yongchang commandery, source of many exotic goods.

sentences.zh: 大秦西海水之西有河，河西南流。

translations.literal: West of Daqin's western sea water there is a river; the river flows southwest.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Western Sea beside Daqin runs a river flowing southwest.

sentences.zh: 河西有南、北山，山西有赤水，西有白玉山。

translations.literal: West of the river are South and North mountains; west of the mountains is Red Water; west is White Jade Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: South and North mountains stand west of the river; beyond them lies the Red Waters, and farther west, White Jade Mountain.

sentences.zh: 玉山西有西王母山，玉為堂云。

translations.literal: West of Jade Mountain is Queen Mother of the West Mountain; jade is said to serve as halls.
translations.idiomatic: West of that mountain rises Mount Queen Mother of the West, where halls are said to be built of jade.

sentences.zh: 從安息西界循海曲，亦至大秦，回萬餘里。

translations.literal: From Parthia's western border following the sea's curve, one also reaches Daqin—a roundabout of more than ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: From Parthia's western frontier along the coast one can also reach Daqin—a roundabout journey of over ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: [22]於彼國觀日月星辰，無異中國，而前史云條支西行百里日入處，失之遠矣。

translations.literal: [22] Observing sun, moon, and stars in that country, there is no difference from China—yet former histories say west of Tiaozhi one hundred li is where the sun sets; that is far off the mark.
translations.idiomatic: [22] The heavens over Daqin match China's—the old claim that the sun sets a hundred li west of Tiaozhi falls far short of the truth.

sentences.zh: 阿鈎羌國，在莎車西南，去代一萬三千里。

translations.literal: The state of Agouqiang lies southwest of Yarkand, thirteen thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Agouqiang, southwest of Yarkand, lies thirteen thousand li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 國西有縣度山，其間四百里中，往往有棧道，下臨不測之淵，人行以繩索相持而度，因以名之。

translations.literal: West of the state is Xiandu Mountain; within four hundred li between, here and there are plank roads overlooking unfathomable abysses—travelers cross holding one another by rope, and from this it takes its name.
translations.idiomatic: Xiandu Mountain lies to the west; for four hundred li cliffside paths over bottomless gorges require travelers to cross on ropes—hence the name "Suspended Crossing."

sentences.zh: 土有五穀諸果。

translations.literal: The soil has the five grains and various fruits.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and many fruits grow there.

sentences.zh: 巿用錢為貨。

translations.literal: In markets they use coins as currency.
translations.idiomatic: Markets trade in coin.

sentences.zh: 居止立宮室。

translations.literal: In dwelling they erect palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: They build permanent dwellings and halls.

sentences.zh: 有兵器。

translations.literal: They have weapons.
translations.idiomatic: They maintain arms.

sentences.zh: 土出金珠。

translations.literal: The soil produces gold and pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and pearls come from its soil.

sentences.zh: 波路國，在阿鈎羌西北，去代一萬三千九百里。

translations.literal: The state of Bolu lies northwest of Agouqiang, thirteen thousand nine hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Bolu, northwest of Agouqiang, lies thirteen thousand nine hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其地濕熱，有蜀馬，土平，物產國俗與阿鈎羌同。

translations.literal: Its land is damp and hot; it has Shu horses; the soil is level; products, customs, and state ways are the same as Agouqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Humid and hot, with level land and Shu-bred horses; its products and customs match Agouqiang's.

sentences.zh: 小月氏國，都富樓沙城。

translations.literal: The state of the Lesser Yuezhi—capital Fulousha City.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Yuezhi have their capital at Fulousha.

sentences.zh: 其王本大月氏王寄多羅子也。

translations.literal: Its king was originally the son of the Great Yuezhi king Jiduoluo.
translations.idiomatic: Its king was a son of Jiduoluo, ruler of the Great Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 寄多羅為匈奴所逐，[23]西徙後令其子守此城，因號小月氏焉。

translations.literal: Jiduoluo was driven out by the Xiongnu; [23] after moving west he ordered his son to guard this city, and thus it was called the Lesser Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Driven out by the Xiongnu, [23] Jiduoluo moved west and left his son to hold this city—whence the name Lesser Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 在波路西南，去代一萬六千六百里。

translations.literal: It lies southwest of Bolu, sixteen thousand six hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of Bolu, sixteen thousand six hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 先居西平、張掖之間，被服頗與羌同。

translations.literal: Formerly they dwelt between Xiping and Zhangye; dress and apparel are largely the same as the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: They once lived between Xiping and Zhangye; their dress resembles the Qiang's.

sentences.zh: 其俗以金銀錢為貨。

translations.literal: Their custom uses gold and silver coins as currency.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and silver coin serve as currency.

sentences.zh: 隨畜牧移徙，亦類匈奴。

translations.literal: Following livestock they move and migrate; they also resemble the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Pastoral nomads, their ways resemble the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 其城東十里有佛塔，周三百五十步，高八十丈。

translations.literal: Ten li east of its city is a Buddhist pagoda, circumference three hundred fifty paces, height eighty zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li east of the city stands a Buddhist pagoda three hundred fifty paces around and eighty zhang high.

sentences.zh: 自佛塔初建，計至武定八年，八百四十二年，所謂「百丈佛圖」也。

translations.literal: From the pagoda's first construction, reckoning to the eighth year of Wuding, eight hundred forty-two years—the so-called "Hundred-Zhang Buddha Tower."
translations.idiomatic: From its founding to Wuding 8 (550 CE) was eight hundred forty-two years—the famed "Hundred-Zhang Pagoda."

sentences.zh: 罽賓國，都善見城，在波路西南，去代一萬四千二百里。

translations.literal: The state of Kashmir—capital Shanxian City—lies southwest of Bolu, fourteen thousand two hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Kashmir (Jibin), capital at Shanxian, lies southwest of Bolu, fourteen thousand two hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 居在四山中。

translations.literal: It dwells within four mountains.
translations.idiomatic: It lies enclosed by four mountain ranges.

sentences.zh: 其地東西八百里，南北三百里。

translations.literal: Its territory is eight hundred li east-west, three hundred li north-south.
translations.idiomatic: The realm measures eight hundred li east to west and three hundred north to south.

sentences.zh: 地平溫和。

translations.literal: The land is level and mild.
translations.idiomatic: Level terrain and a mild climate.

sentences.zh: 有苜蓿、雜草、奇木、檀、槐、梓、竹。

translations.literal: It has alfalfa, miscellaneous grasses, rare trees, sandalwood, locust, catalpa, and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Alfalfa and mixed pasture grow there, with sandalwood, locust, catalpa, bamboo, and other fine timber.

sentences.zh: 種五穀，糞園田。

translations.literal: They plant the five grains and manure garden fields.
translations.idiomatic: They farm grain and fertilize their gardens.

sentences.zh: 地下濕，生稻。

translations.literal: The ground below is damp; rice grows.
translations.idiomatic: Damp soil supports rice cultivation.

sentences.zh: 冬食生菜。

translations.literal: In winter they eat raw vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Raw greens are eaten even in winter.

sentences.zh: 其人工巧，雕文、刻鏤、織罽。

translations.literal: Its people are skilled in craft—carving patterns, incising and piercing, weaving felt rugs.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen excel at carved ornament, inlay work, and felt weaving.

sentences.zh: 有金銀銅錫以為器物。

translations.literal: They have gold, silver, copper, and tin for making vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, copper, and tin serve for utensils.

sentences.zh: 巿用錢。

translations.literal: Markets use coin.
translations.idiomatic: Coin is the market currency.

sentences.zh: 他畜與諸國同。

translations.literal: Other livestock are the same as in various states.
translations.idiomatic: Other livestock match those of neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 每使朝獻。

translations.literal: On each mission they come to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: It sends tribute with every embassy.

sentences.zh: 吐呼羅國，去代一萬二千里。

translations.literal: The state of Tuhuoluo is twelve thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhuoluo lies twelve thousand li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 東至范陽國，西至悉萬斤國，中間相去二千里；

translations.literal: East to the state of Fanyang, west to the state of Samarkand—the distance between is two thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: Fanyang lies two thousand li to the east, Samarkand to the west;

sentences.zh: 南至連山，不知名；

translations.literal: South to linked mountains, names unknown;
translations.idiomatic: Unnamed mountain chains mark the southern border;

sentences.zh: 北至波斯國，中間相去一萬里。

translations.literal: North to the state of Persia—the distance between is ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Persia lies ten thousand li to the north.

sentences.zh: 國中有薄提城，周帀六十里。

translations.literal: Within the state is Boti City, circumference sixty li all around.
translations.idiomatic: Its chief city Boti has walls sixty li around.

sentences.zh: 城南有西流大水，名漢樓河。

translations.literal: South of the city is a great river flowing west, named the Hanlou River.
translations.idiomatic: A great river flowing west past the city's south is called the Hanlou.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀，有好馬、駝、騾。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains; there are fine horses, camels, and mules.
translations.idiomatic: Grain thrives; fine horses, camels, and mules are raised.

sentences.zh: 其王曾遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Its king once sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Its king has sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 副貨國，去代一萬七千里。

translations.literal: The state of Fuhe is seventeen thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhe lies seventeen thousand li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 東至阿副使且國，西至沒誰國，中間相去一千里；

translations.literal: East to the state of Afushiqie, west to the state of Meishui—the distance between is one thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: Afushiqie lies a thousand li to the east, Meishui to the west;

sentences.zh: 南有連山，不知名；

translations.literal: South there are linked mountains, names unknown;
translations.idiomatic: Unnamed ranges lie to the south;

sentences.zh: 北至奇沙國，相去一千五百里。

translations.literal: North to the state of Qisha—the distance is one thousand five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Qisha is fifteen hundred li to the north.

sentences.zh: 國中有副貨城，周帀七十里。

translations.literal: Within the state is Fuhe City, circumference seventy li all around.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhe city within the realm has walls seventy li around.

sentences.zh: 宜五穀、萄桃，唯有馬、駝、騾。

translations.literal: Suited to the five grains and grapes; it has only horses, camels, and mules.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and grapes grow there; horses, camels, and mules are its chief livestock.

sentences.zh: 國王有黃金殿，殿下金駝七頭，各高三尺。

translations.literal: The state king has a golden hall; beneath the hall seven golden camels, each three chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The king's golden hall stands flanked by seven gilded camels, each three feet tall.

sentences.zh: 其王遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Its king sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Its king has sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 南天竺

translations.literal: South India.
translations.idiomatic: South India.

sentences.zh: 南天竺國，去代三萬一千五百里。

translations.literal: The state of South India is thirty-one thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: South India lies thirty-one thousand five hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 有伏醜城，周帀十里，城中出摩尼珠、[24]珊瑚。

translations.literal: It has Fuchou City, ten li in circumference; within the city are produced mani pearls, [24] and coral.
translations.idiomatic: Its Fuchou city, ten li around the walls, yields mani pearls, [24] coral, and other treasures.

sentences.zh: 城東三百里有拔賴城，城中出黃金、白真檀、石蜜、蒲萄。

translations.literal: Three hundred li east of the city is Balai City; within it are produced gold, white sandalwood, rock honey, and grapes.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li east stands Balai city, which produces gold, white sandalwood, rock honey, and grapes.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Grain crops grow well there.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，其國王婆羅化遣使獻駿馬、金、銀，自此每使朝貢。

translations.literal: During Emperor Shizong's time, its king Poluohua sent envoys presenting fine horses, gold, and silver; from then on envoys came with tribute on every occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu its king Poluohua sent envoys with fine horses, gold, and silver; thereafter tribute missions arrived regularly.

sentences.zh: 疊伏羅國，去代三萬一千里。

translations.literal: The state of Diefuluo is thirty-one thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Diefuluo lies thirty-one thousand li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 國中有勿悉城。

translations.literal: Within the state is Wuxi City.
translations.idiomatic: The state contains Wuxi city.

sentences.zh: 城北有鹽奇水，西流。

translations.literal: North of the city is the Yanqi River, which flows west.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city the Yanqi River runs westward.

sentences.zh: 有白象，并有阿末黎，木皮中織作布。

translations.literal: There are white elephants; there is also amali, whose bark is woven within to make cloth.
translations.idiomatic: White elephants are found there, and the bark of the amali tree is woven into cloth.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Grain crops grow well there.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，其國王伏陀末多遣使獻方物，自是每使朝貢。

translations.literal: During Emperor Shizong's time, its king Fotuomoduo sent envoys presenting local products; from then on envoys came with tribute on every occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu its king Fotuomoduo sent envoys with local goods, and tribute missions followed thereafter.

sentences.zh: 拔豆國，去代五萬一千里。

translations.literal: The state of Badou is fifty-one thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Badou lies fifty-one thousand li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 東至多勿當國，西至旃那國，中間相去七百五十里；

translations.literal: East to the state of Duobudang, west to the state of Zhanna—the distance between them is seven hundred fifty li;
translations.idiomatic: It extends seven hundred fifty li from Duobudang in the east to Zhanna in the west;

sentences.zh: 南至罽陵伽國，北至弗那伏且國，中間相去九百里。

translations.literal: South to the state of Jilingjia, north to the state of Funafuqie—the distance between them is nine hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: and nine hundred li from Jilingjia in the south to Funafuqie in the north.

sentences.zh: 國中出金、銀、雜寶、白象、水牛、氂牛、蒲萄、五果。

translations.literal: Within the state are produced gold, silver, assorted treasures, white elephants, water buffalo, yaks, grapes, and the five fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The country yields gold, silver, mixed gems, white elephants, water buffalo, yaks, grapes, and many kinds of fruit.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Grain crops grow well there.

sentences.zh: 嚈噠國，大月氏之種類也，亦曰高車之別種，其原出於塞北。

translations.literal: The state of the Hephthalites is a branch of the Great Yuezhi; it is also said to be a separate branch of the Gaoche; its origins lie north of the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Hephthalites were kin to the Great Yuezhi and are also described as an offshoot of the Gaoche, originating north of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 自金山而南，在于闐之西，都烏許水南二百餘里，[25]去長安一萬一百里。

translations.literal: From Mount Jin southward, west of Khotan, its capital is two hundred-odd li south of the Wuxu River, [25] ten thousand one hundred li from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: South of Mount Jin and west of Khotan, their capital stood two hundred-odd li south of the Wuxu River, [25] ten thousand one hundred li from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 其王都拔底延城，蓋王舍城也。

translations.literal: The king's capital is Baditing City—presumably Rajagriha.
translations.idiomatic: Their royal seat was Baditing city, thought to be the same as Rajagriha.

sentences.zh: 其城方十里餘，多寺塔，皆飾以金。

translations.literal: Its city is a little more than ten li square; there are many temples and pagodas, all adorned with gold.
translations.idiomatic: The city measured somewhat more than ten li on a side, with many temples and pagodas gilded throughout.

sentences.zh: 風俗與突厥略同。

translations.literal: Customs are roughly the same as those of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs broadly resembled those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 其俗兄弟共一妻，夫無兄弟者其妻戴一角帽，若有兄弟者依其多少之數，更加角焉。

translations.literal: Their custom is for brothers to share one wife; if a husband has no brothers, his wife wears a one-horned cap; if he has brothers, horns are added according to their number.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers shared one wife: a wife whose husband had no brothers wore a cap with a single horn, and one horn was added for each brother he had.

sentences.zh: 衣服類加以纓絡。

translations.literal: Garments are somewhat adorned with tassels and chains.
translations.idiomatic: Their dress was hung with tassels and chains.

sentences.zh: [26]頭皆剪髮。

translations.literal: [26] All cut their hair short.
translations.idiomatic: [26] They all wore their hair cropped short.

sentences.zh: 其語與蠕蠕、高車及諸胡不同。

translations.literal: Their language differs from that of the Rouran, the Gaoche, and the various Hu peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Their language differed from Rouran, Gaoche, and the other western peoples.

sentences.zh: 眾可十萬。

translations.literal: The population may reach one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Their numbers ran to about one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 無城邑，依隨水草，以氈為屋，夏遷涼土，冬逐暖處。

translations.literal: They have no walled settlements; they follow water and pasture, using felt for dwellings; in summer they move to cool lands, in winter they seek warm places.
translations.idiomatic: They had no walled towns but followed pasture and water, living in felt tents and moving to cooler ground in summer and warmer ground in winter.

sentences.zh: 分其諸妻，各在別所，相去或二百、三百里。

translations.literal: The king's wives are dispersed, each at a separate place, two or three hundred li apart.
translations.idiomatic: His wives were kept apart in separate camps, sometimes two or three hundred li from one another.

sentences.zh: 其王巡歷而行，每月一處，冬寒之時，三月不徙。

translations.literal: The king travels on circuit, one place each month; in the cold of winter he does not move for three months.
translations.idiomatic: The king toured his realm, spending a month at each stop, and in the depth of winter he remained in one place for three months.

sentences.zh: 王位不必傳子，子弟堪任，死便授之。

translations.literal: The throne need not pass to a son; whichever kinsman is fit receives it upon death.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not necessarily pass to a son: when the king died, it went to whichever relative was deemed capable.

sentences.zh: 其國無車有輿。

translations.literal: The state has no carts but has palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: They had no wheeled carts but used palanquins.

sentences.zh: 多駝馬。

translations.literal: Camels and horses are numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Camels and horses were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 用刑嚴急，偷盜無多少皆腰斬，盜一責十。

translations.literal: Punishments are harsh and swift; for theft, regardless of amount, the waist is cut; one theft requires tenfold restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Their punishments were severe: any theft, however small, meant execution by cutting at the waist, and restitution at ten times the value.

sentences.zh: 死者，富者累石為藏，貧者掘地而埋，隨身諸物，皆置冢內。

translations.literal: When someone dies, the rich pile stones for a tomb, the poor dig earth to bury; all personal goods are placed within the mound.
translations.idiomatic: The rich built stone tombs for the dead and the poor buried them in the earth, placing all their personal belongings in the grave.

sentences.zh: 其人兇悍，能鬬戰。

translations.literal: Its people are fierce and capable in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They were a fierce people and skilled fighters.

sentences.zh: 西域康居、于闐、沙勒、安息及諸小國三十許皆役屬之，號為大國。

translations.literal: In the Western Regions, Kangju, Khotan, Kashgar, Parthia, and some thirty smaller states all served and submitted to them; they were called a great state.
translations.idiomatic: Some thirty states of the west, including Kangju, Khotan, Kashgar, and Parthia, were subject to them, and they were reckoned a great power.

sentences.zh: 與蠕蠕婚姻。

translations.literal: They intermarried with the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: They intermarried with the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 自太安以後，每遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: From the Tai'an era onward, they sent envoys with tribute on every occasion.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tai'an era they sent regular tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 正光末，遣使貢師子一，至高平，遇万俟醜奴反，因留之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang, they sent envoys presenting one lion; reaching Gaoping, they encountered Moqi Chounu's rebellion and were detained.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhengguang era they sent a lion as tribute; at Gaoping they were caught up in Moqi Chounu's rebellion and detained.

sentences.zh: 醜奴平，送京師。

translations.literal: When Chounu was suppressed, it was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Chounu was defeated, the lion was sent on to the capital.

sentences.zh: 永熙以後，朝獻遂絕。

translations.literal: After Yongxi, court tribute ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongxi era tribute missions ceased altogether.

sentences.zh: 其國南去漕國千五百里，東去瓜州六千五百里。

translations.literal: From this state south to Caoguo is one thousand five hundred li; east to Guazhou is six thousand five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: It lay fifteen hundred li south of Caoguo and sixty-five hundred li east of Guazhou.

translations.literal: Footnote [27].
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note [27].

sentences.zh: 初，熙平中，肅宗遣王伏子統宋雲、沙門法力等使西域，[28]訪求佛經。

translations.literal: At first, during Xiping, Emperor Suzong sent Wang Fuzi to lead Song Yun, the monk Fali, and others on a mission to the Western Regions, [28] to seek Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Xiping era, Emperor Xiaoming dispatched Wang Fuzi to lead Song Yun, the monk Fali, and others westward [28] in search of Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 時有沙門慧生者亦與俱行，正光中還。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Huisheng also traveled with them; he returned during Zhengguang.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huisheng traveled with them and returned in the Zhengguang era.

sentences.zh: 慧生所經諸國，不能知其本末及山川里數，蓋舉其略云。

translations.literal: Of the states Huisheng passed through, one cannot know their full origins or the distances of mountains and rivers; this account gives only a summary.
translations.idiomatic: For the countries Huisheng visited, the full history and exact distances cannot be known; what follows is only a summary of his account.

sentences.zh: 朱居國，[29]在于闐西。

translations.literal: The state of Zhuju, [29] lies west of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuju, [29] lay west of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 其人山居。

translations.literal: Its people dwell in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Its people lived in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 有麥，多林果。

translations.literal: There is wheat; forest fruits are abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat was grown there, and forest fruits were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 咸事佛。

translations.literal: All serve the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: All were Buddhist.

sentences.zh: 語與于闐相類。

translations.literal: The language resembles that of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Their language resembled Khotan's.

sentences.zh: 役屬嚈噠。

translations.literal: It serves and is subject to the Hephthalites.
translations.idiomatic: It was subject to the Hephthalites.

sentences.zh: 渴槃陁國，在葱嶺東，朱駒波西。

translations.literal: The state of Kepantuo lies east of the Pamirs and west of Zhujubo.
translations.idiomatic: Kepantuo lay east of the Pamirs and west of Zhujubo.

sentences.zh: 河經其國，東北流。

translations.literal: A river passes through the state and flows northeast.
translations.idiomatic: A river ran through the country and flowed northeast.

sentences.zh: 有高山，夏積霜雪。

translations.literal: There are high mountains; in summer frost and snow accumulate.
translations.idiomatic: High mountains there still held frost and snow even in summer.

sentences.zh: 亦事佛道。

translations.literal: They also serve the Buddhist Way.
translations.idiomatic: They too were Buddhist.

sentences.zh: 附於嚈噠。

translations.literal: Attached to the Hephthalites.
translations.idiomatic: They were attached to the Hephthalites.

sentences.zh: 鉢和國，在渴槃陁西。

translations.literal: The state of Bohe lies west of Kepantuo.
translations.idiomatic: Bohe lay west of Kepantuo.

sentences.zh: 其土尤寒，人畜同居，穴地而處。

translations.literal: Its land is extremely cold; people and livestock dwell together, living in excavated underground dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: The land was bitterly cold; people and livestock shared underground dwellings dug into the earth.

sentences.zh: 又有大雪山，望若銀峯。

translations.literal: There is also a great snow mountain, which seen from afar resembles a silver peak.
translations.idiomatic: A great snow peak rose there, gleaming like silver from a distance.

sentences.zh: 其人唯食餅麨，飲麥酒，服氊裘。

translations.literal: Its people eat only flatbread and roasted flour cakes, drink barley wine, and wear felt furs.
translations.idiomatic: They lived on flatbread and roasted flour, drank barley wine, and wore felt furs.

sentences.zh: 有二道，一道西行向嚈噠，一道西南趣烏萇。

translations.literal: There are two routes: one goes west toward the Hephthalites; one goes southwest toward Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Two roads led out: one west toward the Hephthalites, another southwest toward Gandhara.

sentences.zh: 亦為嚈噠所統。

translations.literal: It is also ruled by the Hephthalites.
translations.idiomatic: It too was under Hephthalite rule.

sentences.zh: 波知國，在鉢和西南。

translations.literal: The state of Bozhi lies southwest of Bohe.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi lay southwest of Bohe.

sentences.zh: 土狹人貧，依託山谷，其王不能總攝。

translations.literal: The land is narrow and the people poor; they rely on mountain valleys; the king cannot govern them all.
translations.idiomatic: The land was cramped and the people poor, clinging to mountain valleys beyond their king's full control.

sentences.zh: 有三池，傳云大池有龍王，次者有龍婦，小者有龍子，行人經之，設祭乃得過，不祭多遇風雪之困。

translations.literal: There are three pools; tradition says the great pool has a dragon king, the middle a dragon queen, and the small a dragon prince; travelers passing them must offer sacrifice to get through—without sacrifice they often meet hardship from wind and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Three pools lay along the route; legend held that the largest held a dragon king, the next a dragon queen, and the smallest a dragon prince. Travelers had to make offerings to pass safely; without them they often met blizzards and hardship.

sentences.zh: 賒彌國，在波知之南。

translations.literal: The state of Shemi lies south of Bozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shemi lay south of Bozhi.

sentences.zh: 山居。

translations.literal: Mountain dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Its people lived in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 不信佛法，專事諸神。

translations.literal: They do not believe in the Buddhist Dharma but devote themselves exclusively to various gods.
translations.idiomatic: They did not follow Buddhism but worshipped their own gods.

sentences.zh: 亦附嚈噠。

translations.literal: Also attached to the Hephthalites.
translations.idiomatic: They too were attached to the Hephthalites.

sentences.zh: 東有鉢盧勒國，[30]路嶮，緣鐵鎖而度，下不見底。

translations.literal: East is the state of Bolule; [30] the road is perilous, crossed by clinging to iron chains, with the bottom not visible below.
translations.idiomatic: East lay Bolule, [30] where the road was treacherous: travelers crossed on iron chains with the abyss hidden below.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，宋雲等竟不能達。

translations.literal: During Xiping, Song Yun and the others in the end could not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiping era Song Yun's party never reached it.

sentences.zh: 烏萇國，在賒彌南。

translations.literal: The state of Wuchang lies south of Shemi.
translations.idiomatic: Gandhara lay south of Shemi.

sentences.zh: 北有葱嶺，南至天竺。

translations.literal: North are the Pamirs; south to India.
translations.idiomatic: The Pamirs lay to the north and India to the south.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門胡為其上族。

translations.literal: Brahman Hu form its upper clan.
translations.idiomatic: Brahmins formed the ruling elite.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門多解天文吉凶之數，其王動則訪決焉。

translations.literal: Brahmins mostly understand the reckonings of astronomy and good and ill fortune; when the king acts he consults them for decisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Brahmins were versed in astronomy and omens, and the king consulted them before any major move.

sentences.zh: 土多林果，引水灌田，豐稻麥。

translations.literal: The land has many forest fruits; water is drawn to irrigate fields; rice and wheat are abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Fruit trees were plentiful, fields were irrigated, and rice and wheat flourished.

sentences.zh: 事佛，多諸寺塔，事極華麗。

translations.literal: They serve the Buddha; there are many temples and pagodas, done with utmost splendor.
translations.idiomatic: They were devout Buddhists, with many temples and pagodas of extraordinary splendor.

sentences.zh: 人有爭訴，服之以藥，曲者發狂，直者無恙。

translations.literal: When people have disputes, they are made to take a drug; the guilty go mad, the innocent are unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Disputes were settled by ordeal: both parties took a drug, and the guilty went mad while the innocent suffered no harm.

sentences.zh: 為法不殺，犯死罪唯徙於靈山。

translations.literal: By their law they do not kill; those guilty of capital crimes are only exiled to Ling Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Their law forbade execution; capital offenders were banished to Ling Mountain.

sentences.zh: [31]西南有檀特山，山上立寺，以驢數頭運食，山下無人控御，自知往來也。

translations.literal: [31] Southwest is Tante Mountain; a temple stands on the mountain; several donkeys carry food—below the mountain no one guides them, yet they know to go back and forth by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: [31] Southwest stood Tante Mountain, with a temple on its summit where several donkeys carried provisions; though no one guided them from below, they came and went on their own.

sentences.zh: 乾陀國，在烏萇西，本名業波，為嚈噠所破，因改焉。

translations.literal: The state of Gandhara lies west of Wuchang; its original name was Yabo; it was destroyed by the Hephthalites and therefore changed.
translations.idiomatic: Gandhara lay west of Wuchang; formerly called Yabo, it was conquered by the Hephthalites and renamed.

sentences.zh: 其王本是敕勒，臨國已二世矣。

translations.literal: Its king was originally of the Tiele; he has ruled the state for two generations already.
translations.idiomatic: Its king was a Tiele by origin and had ruled for two generations.

sentences.zh: [32]好征戰，與罽賓鬬，三年不罷，人怨苦之。

translations.literal: [32] Fond of campaigning, he fought with Kapisa for three years without cease; the people resented and suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: [32] He loved war and fought Kapisa for three unbroken years, to the people's bitter distress.

sentences.zh: 有鬬象七百頭，十人乘一象，皆執兵仗，象鼻縳刀以戰。

translations.literal: There are seven hundred war elephants; ten men ride each elephant, all bearing weapons; knives are bound to the elephants' trunks for battle.
translations.idiomatic: He fielded seven hundred war elephants, ten men to each, all armed; blades were lashed to the elephants' trunks for combat.

sentences.zh: 所都城東南七里有佛塔，高七十丈，周三百步，即所謂「雀離佛圖」也。

translations.literal: Seven li southeast of the capital city is a Buddhist pagoda, seventy zhang high and three hundred paces in circumference—the so-called "Que-li Buddhist Tower."
translations.idiomatic: Seven li southeast of the capital stood a pagoda seventy zhang tall and three hundred paces around—the famed "Que-li" stupa.

sentences.zh: 康國者，康居之後也。

translations.literal: Kang is the successor of Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was the heir state of Kangju.

sentences.zh: 遷徙無常，不恒故地，自漢以來，相承不絕。

translations.literal: Its migrations are without fixed pattern; it does not remain in its old lands; from Han times onward, succession has never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: It moved often and held no fixed territory, yet had endured in succession since Han times.

sentences.zh: 其王本姓溫，月氏人也。

translations.literal: Its king's original surname is Wen; he is a man of the Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: The royal clan bore the surname Wen and were of Yuezhi descent.

sentences.zh: 舊居祁連山北昭武城，因被匈奴所破，西踰葱嶺，遂有其國。

translations.literal: They formerly dwelt at Zhaowu City north of the Qilian Mountains; because they were destroyed by the Xiongnu, they crossed west over the Pamirs and thus came to possess this state.
translations.idiomatic: They once lived at Zhaowu city north of the Qilian range; driven out by the Xiongnu, they crossed the Pamirs westward and established their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 枝庶各分王，故康國左右諸國，並以昭武為姓，示不忘本也。

translations.literal: Branches and cadets each ruled separately; therefore the states to left and right of Kang all take Zhaowu as surname, showing that they do not forget their origins.
translations.idiomatic: Cadet branches ruled neighboring states, and the kingdoms around Kang all took Zhaowu as their surname to remember their origins.

sentences.zh: 王字世夫畢，為人寬厚，甚得眾心。

translations.literal: The king's style is Shifubi; as a man he is generous and mild, and greatly wins the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: The king, styled Shifubi, was generous and won deep loyalty from his people.

sentences.zh: 其妻突厥達度可汗女也。

translations.literal: His wife is the daughter of the Turk khan Tardu.
translations.idiomatic: His queen was a daughter of the Turk khan Tardu.

sentences.zh: 都於薩寶水上阿祿迪城，多人居。

translations.literal: The capital is Aludi City on the Sabao River; many people dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was Aludi city on the Sabao River, thickly populated.

sentences.zh: 大臣三人共掌國事。

translations.literal: Three great ministers jointly administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three chief ministers shared governance of the realm.

sentences.zh: 其王索髮，冠七寶金花，衣綾、羅、錦、繡、白疊；

translations.literal: The king wears his hair loose, crowns himself with a seven-jewel golden flower, and dresses in gauze, silk, brocade, embroidery, and white layered cloth;
translations.idiomatic: The king wore his hair loose, a crown of seven-jeweled gold flowers, and robes of gauze, silk, brocade, embroidery, and white layered cloth;

sentences.zh: 其妻有髻，幪以皂巾。

translations.literal: His wife has a topknot, veiled with a black cloth.
translations.idiomatic: his queen wore a topknot veiled in black cloth.

sentences.zh: 丈夫翦髮，錦袍。

translations.literal: Husbands cut their hair short and wear brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: Men cropped their hair and wore brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 名為強國，西域諸國多歸之。

translations.literal: It is called a strong state; many states of the Western Regions submit to it.
translations.idiomatic: It was reckoned a great power, and many western states acknowledged its sway.

sentences.zh: 米國、史國、曹國、何國、安國、小安國、那色波國、烏那曷國、穆國皆歸附之。

translations.literal: Mi, Shi, Cao, He, An, Xiao'an, Nasabo, Wunahe, and Mu all submit and attach themselves to it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, Shi, Cao, He, An, Lesser An, Nasabo, Wunahe, and Mu all came under its authority.

sentences.zh: 有胡律，置於祅祠，將決罰，則取而斷之。

translations.literal: There are foreign laws, placed in the fire temple; when about to decide punishment, they take them out and pronounce judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign laws were kept in the fire temple; when cases came to judgment, the priests took them out and pronounced sentence.

sentences.zh: 重者族，次罪者死，賊盜截其足。

translations.literal: For serious offenses, the whole clan; for secondary offenses, death; thieves and robbers have their feet amputated.
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes brought extinction of the clan; lesser felonies meant death; thieves and robbers lost their feet.

sentences.zh: 人皆深目、高鼻、多髯。

translations.literal: The people all have deep-set eyes, high noses, and heavy beards.
translations.idiomatic: The people were deep-eyed, high-nosed, and bearded.

sentences.zh: 善商賈，諸夷交易多湊其國。

translations.literal: They are skilled in commerce; trade among the various barbarians largely gathers in their state.
translations.idiomatic: They were adept merchants, and trade from many foreign peoples flowed through their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 有大小鼓、琵琶、五弦箜篌。

translations.literal: There are large and small drums, pipa, and five-string konghou.
translations.idiomatic: Music included large and small drums, pipa lutes, and five-stringed harps.

sentences.zh: 婚姻喪制與突厥同。

translations.literal: Marriage and mourning institutions are the same as the Turks'.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage customs and funeral rites matched those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 國立祖廟，以六月祭之，諸國皆助祭。

translations.literal: The state establishes an ancestral temple and sacrifices to it in the sixth month; all states assist at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The realm maintained an ancestral temple, sacrificed in the sixth month, and other states sent offerings to join the rite.

sentences.zh: 奉佛為胡書。

translations.literal: They revere the Buddha; their writing is foreign script.
translations.idiomatic: They were Buddhist and wrote in a foreign script.

sentences.zh: 氣候溫，宜五穀，勤修園蔬，樹木滋茂。

translations.literal: The climate is warm, suited to the five grains; they diligently cultivate garden vegetables; trees flourish abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was mild and good for grain; gardens were carefully tended and the trees grew thick.

sentences.zh: 出馬、駝、驢、犎牛、黃金、硇沙、[33]𧵊香、阿薛那香、瑟瑟、麞皮、氍毹、錦、疊。

translations.literal: It produces horses, camels, donkeys, zebu cattle, gold, sal ammoniac, [33] benzoin, ashina incense, lapis lazuli, deer hide, carpets, brocade, and layered cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Exports included horses, camels, donkeys, and zebu; gold, sal ammoniac, [33] benzoin, ashina incense, and lapis lazuli; deer hides, carpets, brocades, and layered silks.

sentences.zh: 多蒲萄酒，富家或致十石，連年不敗。

translations.literal: There is much grape wine; wealthy families sometimes stock ten shi; for successive years it does not spoil.
translations.idiomatic: Grape wine was plentiful; rich households sometimes laid down ten shi that would keep for years without turning.

sentences.zh: 太延中，[34]始遣使貢方物，後遂絕焉。

translations.literal: In the Taiyan era, [34] they first sent envoys to present local products; afterward tribute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyan period, [34] they first sent envoys with local tribute; thereafter the missions stopped.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：西域雖通魏氏，而中原始平，天子方以混一為心，未遑征伐。

translations.literal: The historian states: Although the Western Regions communicated with the Wei house, the Central Plains were not yet pacified; the Son of Heaven's mind was just then on unification, and he had no time for punitive expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Though the western lands had ties with Wei, the heartland was still unsettled and the emperor's aim was unification, leaving no room for distant campaigns.

sentences.zh: 其信使往來，深得羇縻勿絕之道耳。

translations.literal: Their envoys' coming and going thoroughly grasped the way of keeping them attached without severing ties.
translations.idiomatic: Diplomatic exchange alone sufficed—the court had mastered the art of binding them without breaking the bond.

translations.idiomatic: On examination, the Book of Han, juan 96, part 1, Western Regions Account, Shanshan entry reads the cited text; Yan Shigu notes, "the cited text is pronounced yi hu fan."

translations.literal: The Shanshan people quite often plunder them. Note: this sentence does not connect with what precedes; in Tongzhi juan 196, Shanshan entry, above this sentence there are twelve characters "Afterward Wei sent envoys to the Western Regions, passing through their state," which agrees with the preface's statement that Shanshan "then blocked and sealed the road, and Western Regions tribute for successive years did not enter"—suspect this account has lost (those words).
translations.idiomatic: The Shanshan people often plundered them. Note: this sentence does not connect with what precedes; in the Comprehensive Treatises, juan 196, Shanshan entry, twelve characters appear above it—"Afterward Wei sent envoys to the Western Regions, passing through their state"—which matches the preface's remark that Shanshan "then blocked the road, and Western Regions tribute ceased for years." translations.idiomatic: Han Ba, Duke of Jiaozhi, was appointed acting commissioner. All editions write the cited text as the cited text; the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, has the cited text.
