translations.literal: Both read the cited text; no change made.
translations.idiomatic: both read the cited text; no change made.

sentences.zh: 又「首拔」、「樹拔」是一河之異譯，周書有「樹拔」，無「首拔」，北史此傳前半當本魏書，已見「首拔河」，這裏則又採周書，以致複出。

translations.literal: Also Shouba and Shuba are variant translations of one river; Zhoushu has Shuba but not Shouba; the first half of this account in Beishi should originally follow the Book of Wei and already shows Shouba River—here it again draws on Zhoushu, causing duplication.
translations.idiomatic: Shouba and Shuba are variant names for one river; the History of the Zhou has Shuba but not Shouba; the first half of this account in the Northern History should follow the Book of Wei and already mentions the Shouba River—here it draws on the History of the Zhou again, causing duplication.

sentences.zh: 城西五十五里亦有大水 北史卷九七、周書卷五０于闐傳作「十五里」。

translations.literal: Fifty-five li west of the city there is also a great river. The History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, and the History of the Zhou, juan 50, Khotan Account read fifteen li.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-five li west of the city there is also a great river. The History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, and the History of the Zhou, juan 50, Khotan Account read fifteen li.

sentences.zh: 疑上「五」字衍。

translations.literal: Suspect the upper the cited text is spurious.
translations.idiomatic: The initial the cited text is likely spurious.

sentences.zh: 經于闐于闐中于王秋仁輒留之 按語不可解，疑當作「經于闐中，于闐王秋仁輒留之」。

translations.literal: Passing through Khotan, within Khotan, Khotan King Qiuren detained them. Note: the language is unintelligible; suspect it should read "Passing within Khotan, Khotan King Qiuren detained them."
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Khotan, within Khotan, Khotan King Qiuren detained them. Note: the wording is unintelligible; it likely should read, "Passing within Khotan, Khotan King Qiuren detained them."

sentences.zh: 其王號子治呼犍 按漢書卷九六上西域傳上云「西夜國，王號子合王，治呼犍谷」。

translations.literal: Its king's title is Zizhi Hujian. Note: Hanshu juan 96, part 1, Western Regions Account, part 1 says "Xiye State—the king's title is Zihe Wang; he rules Hujian Valley."
translations.idiomatic: Its king's title was Zizhi Hujian. Note: the Book of Han, juan 96, part 1, Western Regions Account says, "Xiye State—the king's title is Zihe Wang; he rules Hujian Valley."

sentences.zh: 這裏「子」下當脫「合」字，但御覽卷七九六

translations.literal: Here under the cited text the character the cited text should be missing; but Imperial Overview juan 796
translations.idiomatic: Here the cited text is likely missing after the cited text; but Imperial Overview, juan 796

sentences.zh: 〈三五三三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 3533〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 3533〉

sentences.zh: 已同今本。

translations.literal: Already agrees with the present text.
translations.idiomatic: already agrees with the present text.

sentences.zh: 鐃沙 諸本及北史卷九七無「鐃」字，周書卷五０、隋書卷八三龜茲傳有。

translations.literal: Bell sand. All editions and Beishi juan 97 lack the cited text; Zhoushu juan 50, Suishu juan 83, Kucha Account has it.
translations.idiomatic: Bell sand. All editions and the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, lack the cited text; the History of the Zhou, juan 50, and the History of the Sui, juan 83, Kucha Account have it.

sentences.zh: 按通典卷一九一龜茲條注引隋西域圖稱白山「即是出碙沙之處」。

translations.literal: On examination, Tongdian juan 191, Kucha entry note citing Sui Western Regions Map says Bai Mountain "is precisely the place that produces bell sand."
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the Comprehensive Institutions, juan 191, Kucha entry note citing the Sui Western Regions Map says Bai Mountain "is precisely where bell sand is produced."

sentences.zh: 「碙」乃「硇」字訛，硇沙即鐃沙。

translations.literal: the cited text is an error for the cited text; sal ammoniac is bell sand.
translations.idiomatic: the cited text is an error for the cited text; sal ammoniac is bell sand.

sentences.zh: 這裏脫「鐃」字，今據補。

translations.literal: Here the cited text is missing; supplied on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: the cited text is missing here; supplied on that basis.

sentences.zh: 東南去瓜州三千一百里 諸本及北史卷九七「三」下無「千一」二字，隋書卷八三龜茲傳有。

translations.literal: Three thousand one hundred li southeast of Guazhou. All editions and Beishi juan 97 lack the cited text after the cited text; Suishu juan 83, Kucha Account has it.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand one hundred li southeast of Guazhou. All editions and the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, lack the cited text after the cited text; the History of the Sui, juan 83, Kucha Account has it.

sentences.zh: 按上云「東去焉耆九百里」，焉耆傳云「西去龜茲九百里，皆沙磧；

translations.literal: On examination, above it says "nine hundred li east to Yanqi"; the Yanqi account says "nine hundred li west to Kucha, all sandy desert;
translations.idiomatic: On examination, above it says "nine hundred li east to Yanqi"; the Yanqi account says "nine hundred li west to Kucha, all sandy desert;

sentences.zh: 東南去瓜州二千二百里」，合計正得三千一百里，知這裏脫「千一」二字，今據隋書補。

translations.literal: "Two thousand two hundred li southeast of Guazhou"-added together this exactly makes three thousand one hundred li; knowing the cited text is missing here; supplied from Suishu."
translations.idiomatic: "two thousand two hundred li southeast of Guazhou"-together these exactly make three thousand one hundred li; the cited text is missing here and is supplied from the History of the Sui."

sentences.zh: 其東

translations.literal: Its east
translations.idiomatic: To its east

translations.literal: 〈Missing text〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Missing text〉

sentences.zh: 城戍 諸本「闕」字作正文，北史卷九七訛作「關」。

translations.literal: fortified garrison. All editions treat the character the cited text as main text; Beishi juan 97 wrongly reads it as the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: is a fortified garrison. All editions treat the cited text as main text; the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, wrongly reads it as the cited text.

sentences.zh: 按「闕」字指「東」下有闕文，本是旁注，誤作正文，今改正。

translations.literal: On examination, the character the cited text indicates missing text below the cited text; it was originally a marginal note, wrongly placed as main text; corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the cited text marks missing text after the cited text; it was originally a marginal note wrongly placed in the main text; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 在迷密西 諸本及北史卷九七「迷」作「悉」，通志卷一九六作「迷」。

translations.literal: West of Mimi. All editions and Beishi juan 97 write the cited text as the cited text; Tongzhi juan 196 has the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: West of Mimi. All editions and the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, write the cited text as the cited text; the Comprehensive Treatises, juan 196, has the cited text.

sentences.zh: 按上條即迷密國，這裏乃涉上兩「悉」字而訛，今據改。

translations.literal: On examination, the entry above is Mimi State; here it was corrupted through the two the cited text characters above; changed on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the entry above is Mimi State; here the text was corrupted by the two the cited text characters above; changed on that basis.

sentences.zh: 洛那國 按傳序及下者舌傳並見「破洛那」，又見卷四上世祖紀上太延三年十一月甲申、卷五高宗紀和平六年四月。

translations.literal: Luona State. Note: the preface and the Zheshe account below both show Poluona; it also appears in juan 4, part 1, Annals of Emperor Shizu, part 1, Taiyan year 3, eleventh month, jiashen; juan 5, Annals of Emperor Gaozong, Heping year 6, fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: Luona State. Note: the preface and the Zheshe account below both read Poluona; it also appears in juan 4, part 1, Annals of Emperor Shizu, Taiyan third year, eleventh month, jiashen, and juan 5, Annals of Emperor Gaozong, Heping sixth year, fourth month.

sentences.zh: 「洛那」上當脫「破」字。

translations.literal: Above Luona the character the cited text should be missing.
translations.idiomatic: the cited text is missing before Luona.

sentences.zh: 太和三年遣使獻汗血馬 按卷七上高祖紀上本年不記此事，而卷四上世祖紀上太延三年十一月甲申稱「破洛那、者舌國各獻汗血馬」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, they sent envoys presenting blood-sweating horses. Note: juan 7, part 1, Annals of Emperor Gaozu, part 1 does not record this in that year; but juan 4, part 1, Annals of Emperor Shizu, part 1, Taiyan year 3, eleventh month, jiashen says "Poluona and Zheshe states each presented blood-sweating horses."
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 3 they sent envoys presenting blood-sweating horses. Note: juan 7, part 1, Annals of Emperor Gaozu does not record this for that year; but juan 4, part 1, Annals of Emperor Shizu, Taiyan third year, eleventh month, jiashen says, "Poluona and Zheshe each presented blood-sweating horses."

sentences.zh: 且傳記通使之始，即使太和有此事，也不當捨「太延」而敍「太和」。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of recording diplomatic contact, even if the Taihe era had such an event, one should not pass over Taiyan and narrate Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when recording the start of diplomatic contact, even if such an event occurred in Taihe, one should not skip Taiyan and narrate Taihe instead.

sentences.zh: 這裏「和」字當是「延」之訛。

translations.literal: Here the character the cited text should be an error for the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: Here the cited text should be an error for the cited text.

sentences.zh: 赤麞皮 隋書卷八三、通典卷一九二、通志卷一九六波斯傳「麞」作「麖」。

translations.literal: Red antelope hide. Suishu juan 83, Tongdian juan 192, Tongzhi juan 196, Persia Account write the cited text as the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: Red antelope hide. The History of the Sui, juan 83; the Comprehensive Institutions, juan 192; and the Comprehensive Treatises, juan 196, Persia Account write the cited text as the cited text.

sentences.zh: 按「麖」乃大鹿，上龜茲傳記土產也有「麖皮」，這裏疑亦作「麖」，後人改作「麞」。

translations.literal: On examination, the cited text is the great deer; the Kucha account above on local products also has the cited text hide; suspect this too should read the cited text, later people changed it to the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the cited text denotes the great deer; the Kucha account above on local products also lists the cited text hide; this likely read the cited text as well, and later hands changed it to the cited text.

sentences.zh: 掌庫藏開禁 周書卷五０波斯傳「開」作「關」。

translations.literal: In charge of treasuries and frontier passes. Zhoushu juan 50, Persia Account writes the cited text as the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: In charge of treasuries and frontier passes. The History of the Zhou, juan 50, Persia Account writes the cited text as the cited text.

sentences.zh: 按此謂掌庫藏及關禁，疑當作「關」。

translations.literal: On examination, this means in charge of treasuries and frontier controls; suspect it should read the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, this means oversight of treasuries and frontier controls; it likely should read the cited text.

sentences.zh: 地卑 諸本及北史卷九七「卑」作「早」。

translations.literal: The land is low-lying. All editions and Beishi juan 97 write the cited text as the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: The land is low-lying. All editions and the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, write the cited text as the cited text.

sentences.zh: 按周書卷五０作「地卑勃」，冊府卷九六二

translations.literal: On examination, Zhoushu juan 50 reads the cited text; Cefu juan 962
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the History of the Zhou, juan 50, reads the cited text; Cefu, juan 962

sentences.zh: 〈一一三一八頁〉
作「地卑」。

translations.literal: reads the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: reads the cited text.

sentences.zh: 北史採周書，冊府此條出北史，知北史本亦作「卑」，「早」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Beishi draws on Zhoushu; this Cefu entry comes from Beishi; knowing Beishi's original also read the cited text; the cited text is an error; changed on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern History draws on the History of the Zhou; this Cefu entry comes from the Northern History; the Northern History originally read the cited text; the cited text is an error; changed on that basis.

sentences.zh: 回萬餘里 諸本「回」作「四」。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand li circuit. All editions write the cited text as the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand li by a winding route. All editions write the cited text as the cited text.

sentences.zh: 據張元濟校勘記，百衲本的底本作「回」，影印時依殿本修。

translations.literal: According to Zhang Yuanji's collation notes, the Patchwork edition's base text reads the cited text; when reprinted it was emended to follow the Palace Edition.
translations.idiomatic: According to Zhang Yuanji's collation notes, the Patchwork edition's base text reads the cited text; the reprint was emended to follow the Palace Edition.

sentences.zh: 按北史卷九七大秦傳作「迴」。

translations.literal: On examination, Beishi juan 97, Da Qin Account reads the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, Da Qin Account reads the cited text.

sentences.zh: 「回」或「迴」意為迂回，「四」字訛，今從百衲本的底本。

translations.literal: the cited text or the cited text means winding/circuitous; the cited text is an error; the text now follows the Patchwork edition's base text.
translations.idiomatic: the cited text or the cited text means winding or circuitous; the cited text is an error; the text now follows the Patchwork edition's base text.

sentences.zh: 寄多羅為匈奴所逐 按大月氏為匈奴所逐，遠在西漢初，見漢書卷九六上西域傳上，這裏所說據上大月氏傳，乃是被「蠕蠕」所侵，才「西徙都薄羅城」。

translations.literal: Jiduoluo was driven out by the Xiongnu. Note: the Great Yuezhi were driven out by the Xiongnu, far back in early Western Han—see Hanshu juan 96, part 1, Western Regions Account, part 1; what is said here draws on the Great Yuezhi account above: they were invaded by the Rouran and only then "migrated west and established their capital at Boluo City."
translations.idiomatic: Jiduoluo was driven out by the Xiongnu. Note: the Great Yuezhi were driven out by the Xiongnu as early as the Western Han—see the Book of Han, juan 96, part 1, Western Regions Account; what is meant here, drawing on the Great Yuezhi account above, is that they were invaded by the Rouran and only then "migrated west and established their capital at Boluo City."

sentences.zh: 「匈奴」應作「蠕蠕」。

translations.literal: "Xiongnu" should read "Rouran."
translations.idiomatic: "Xiongnu" should read "Rouran."

sentences.zh: 城中出摩尼珠 諸本「摩」訛「麾」，今據北史卷九七南天竺國傳、冊府卷九六０

translations.literal: Mani pearls are produced within the city. All editions miswrite the cited text as the cited text; the text now follows Beishi juan 97, South India Account, Cefu juan 960
translations.idiomatic: Mani pearls were produced within the city. All editions miswrite the cited text as the cited text; the text now follows the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, South India Account, and Cefu, juan 960

sentences.zh: 〈一一三０一頁〉
、御覽卷七九三

translations.literal: , Imperial Overview juan 793
translations.idiomatic: , Imperial Overview, juan 793

sentences.zh: 〈三五一五頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 3515〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 3515〉

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Changed.
translations.idiomatic: Emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 都烏許水南二百餘里 諸本「烏」作「馬」。

translations.literal: The capital is more than two hundred li south of the Wuxu River. All editions write the cited text as the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: The capital lies more than two hundred li south of the Wuxu River. All editions read the cited text as the cited text.

sentences.zh: 按烏許、或烏滸水常見紀載，「馬」字顯訛，今據北史卷九七嚈噠傳、隋書卷八三挹怛傳、御覽卷七九三

translations.literal: On examination, Wuxu or Wuhu River appears commonly in records; the character the cited text is clearly erroneous; now changed on the basis of Beishi juan 97, Yanda account, Suishu juan 83, Yidan account, and Yulan juan 793.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxu or Wuhu River is well attested; the cited text is clearly a corruption. The text is emended from the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97 (Hephthalite account), the Book of Sui, juan 83 (Yidan account), and the Imperial Readings, juan 793.

sentences.zh: 〈三五二０頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3520〉

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Changed.
translations.idiomatic: Emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 衣服類加以纓絡 通典卷一九三嚈噠條「類」下有「胡」字，疑當有此字。

translations.literal: Garments are adorned with tassels and chains. Tongdian juan 193, Yanda entry, has the character the cited text below the cited text; it is suspected this character should be present.
translations.idiomatic: Garments are adorned with tassels and chains. The Tongdian, juan 193 (Hephthalite entry), has the cited text after the cited text; that character is probably original.

sentences.zh: 其國南去漕國千五百里東去瓜州六千五百里 此句諸本及北史卷九七都在下文「及山川里數蓋舉其略云」後。

translations.literal: The state is one thousand five hundred li south of Cao and six thousand five hundred li east of Guazhou. This sentence in all editions and Beishi juan 97 all appear after the passage below, "As for mountains, rivers, and distances, this gives only the outline."
translations.idiomatic: The state lies fifteen hundred li south of Cao and sixty-five hundred li east of Guazhou. In all editions and the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, this sentence stands after the line "As for mountains, rivers, and distances, this gives only the outline."

sentences.zh: 按此句是說嚈噠方位，出隋書卷八三挹怛傳。

translations.literal: On examination, this sentence describes the Hephthalites' position and comes from Suishu juan 83, Yidan account.
translations.idiomatic: The line describes Hephthalite geography and derives from the Book of Sui, juan 83 (Yidan account).

sentences.zh: 下文「朱居國」等都是「慧生所經諸國」，此句橫隔其間，不成文體，當是錯簡，今乙正。

translations.literal: Below, "Zhuju State" and the rest are all "states passed through by Huisheng"; this sentence cuts across them and breaks the literary form—it must be displaced text; now transposed to the correct place.
translations.idiomatic: The entries below for Zhuju and the rest belong to "states Huisheng passed through"; this line interrupts them and is displaced text, now moved to its proper place.

sentences.zh: 又諸本脫「南」「東」二字，北史卷九七也脫「南」字，今據隋書挹怛傳補。

translations.literal: Moreover, all editions omit the two characters the cited text and the cited text; Beishi juan 97 also omits the cited text; now supplemented from the Suishu Yidan account.
translations.idiomatic: All editions omit the cited text and the cited text; the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97, also omits the cited text. Both are restored from the Book of Sui, Yidan account.

sentences.zh: 肅宗遣王伏子統宋雲沙門法力等使西域 北史卷九七嚈噠傳「王」作「賸」。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong sent Wang Fuzi to lead the monk Fali of Song Yun and others as envoys to the Western Regions. Beishi juan 97, Yanda account, writes the cited text as the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong dispatched Wang Fuzi to lead Song Yun's monk Fali and others westward. The History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97 (Hephthalite account), reads the cited text as the cited text.

sentences.zh: 按王或賸伏子統均不可解，當有訛脫。

translations.literal: On examination, neither Wang nor Sheng Fuzi Tong is intelligible; there must be corruption or omission.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Wang nor Sheng Fuzi Tong makes sense; the name is corrupt or incomplete.

sentences.zh: 朱居國 按上于闐傳、疏勒傳「朱居」作「朱俱波」，下渴槃陁傳作「朱駒波」，卷八世宗紀景明三年歲末、永平四年九月甲寅作「朱居槃」。

translations.literal: Zhuju State. Note: in the Khotan account and Kashgar account above, the cited text is written the cited text; in the Khotan account below it is the cited text; in juan 8, Annals of Emperor Shizong, end of Jingming year 3 and ninth month, jiayin, of Yongping year 4, it is the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuju State. Above, the Khotan and Kashgar accounts write the cited text; the Khotan account below has the cited text; juan 8, Annals of Emperor Shizong (end of Jingming 3 and Yongping 4.9 jiayin) has the cited text.

sentences.zh: 通典卷一九三朱俱波條云：「朱俱波，後魏時通焉，亦名朱居槃國。」

translations.literal: Tongdian juan 193, Zhujubo entry, says: "Zhujubo had contact in Later Wei times and was also named Zhujupan State."
translations.idiomatic: The Tongdian, juan 193 (Zhujubo entry), states: "Zhujubo had contact in Later Wei times and was also called Zhujupan."

sentences.zh: 譯音出入，本不足怪，但一篇之中，甚至一行之隔，異名錯出，實由北史採取諸書，未加整齊。

translations.literal: Variations in transliteration are not strange in themselves, but within one chapter—even a line apart—different names appear in confusion, truly because the Beishi drew from various books without harmonizing them.
translations.idiomatic: Transliteration varies naturally, but alternate names appear even within a single line because the History of the Northern Dynasties compiled sources without harmonizing them.

sentences.zh: 「朱居槃」未見省稱「朱居」之例，當脫「槃」字。

translations.literal: There is no example of abbreviating the cited text as the cited text; the character the cited text must have been dropped.
translations.idiomatic: the cited text is never shortened to the cited text; the cited text has been dropped.

sentences.zh: 又上文之「悉居半國」，亦即此「朱居槃」之異譯，則前據董琬等所說而此則轉錄宋雲行記，以致重出。

translations.literal: Moreover, "Xijuban State" above is another transliteration of this "Zhujupan"; the former follows Dong Wan and others, while this copies Song Yun's travel record, causing duplication.
translations.idiomatic: Xijuban above is another form of Zhujupan—the earlier passage follows Dong Wan's report, this one Song Yun's travelogue, hence the duplication.

sentences.zh: 東有鉢盧勒國 按「鉢盧勒」即上文之「波路」，此據行記。

translations.literal: To the east is Bolule State. Note: the cited text is Bolu above; this follows the travel record.
translations.idiomatic: Bolule lies to the east-the cited text is the Bolu of the earlier passage, following the travel record.

sentences.zh: 犯死罪唯徙於靈山 洛陽伽藍記卷五載宋雲等行記「靈山」作「空山」。

translations.literal: Those guilty of capital crimes are only exiled to Spirit Mountain. Luoyang qielan ji juan 5, recording Song Yun's travel record, writes the cited text as the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: Capital offenders are exiled to Spirit Mountain. The Record of Buddhist Monasteries of Luoyang, juan 5 (Song Yun's itinerary), reads the cited text as the cited text.

sentences.zh: 臨國已二世矣 諸本「已」訛「民」，今據北史卷九七乾陀傳、伽藍記卷五載行記改。

translations.literal: The state has already had two generations. All editions corrupt the cited text as the cited text; now changed on the basis of Beishi juan 97, Gandhara account, and qielan ji juan 5, travel record.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has seen two generations. All editions miswrite the cited text as the cited text; emended from the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 97 (Gandhara account), and the Record of Buddhist Monasteries, juan 5 (travel record).

sentences.zh: 硇沙 諸本「硇」作「碙」，北史卷九七康國傳百衲本作「𥐻」，北本、汲本作「硇」。

translations.literal: Nao sand. All editions write the cited text as the cited text; Beishi juan 97, Kang account, patchwork edition has the cited text; Northern and Ji editions have the cited text.
translations.idiomatic: Nao sand. Most editions read the cited text as the cited text; the patchwork Beishi, juan 97 (Kang account), has the cited text; the Northern and Ji editions have the cited text.

sentences.zh: 按「碙」乃「硇」之訛，今據北史北、汲本改。

translations.literal: On examination, the cited text is a corruption of the cited text; now changed on the basis of the Northern and Ji editions of Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: the cited text is a corruption of the cited text; emended from the Northern and Ji Beishi editions.

sentences.zh: 參本卷校記

translations.literal: See collation notes to this juan.
translations.idiomatic: See collation notes to this juan.

sentences.zh: 〈一三〉。
太延中 此條全出北史，北史康國條又出隋書，「太延」本作「大業」，後人妄改。

translations.literal: In the Taiyan era. This entry is wholly from Beishi; the Kang entry in Beishi in turn comes from Suishu; the cited text was originally the cited text, wrongly changed by later people.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyan era. This entry is taken entirely from the History of the Northern Dynasties, whose Kang account derives from the Book of Sui; the cited text was originally the cited text and was wrongly altered by later editors.

sentences.zh: 宋人校語已指出。

translations.literal: Song-dynasty collation notes already pointed this out.
translations.idiomatic: Song editors already noted this.
